title: iPhone 18 Pro Max's Larger Battery Capacity Allegedly Revealed
title_bn: iPhone 18 Pro Max's Larger Battery Capacity Allegedly Revealed
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The upcoming iPhone 18 Pro Max will be equipped with a nearly 12% larger battery compared to the iPhone 17 Pro Max, according to an apparent leak. An alleged photo of a battery pack for a Chinese model of the iPhone 18 Pro Max with a SIM card tray li
paragraph1: The upcoming iPhone 18 Pro Max will be equipped with a nearly 12% larger battery compared to the iPhone 17 Pro Max, according to an apparent leak. An alleged photo of a battery pack for a Chinese model of the iPhone 18 Pro Max with a SIM card tray lists a capacity of 5,391 mAh, up from 4,823 mAh for the equivalent iPhone 17 Pro Max battery. The photo was shared on the Korean platform Naver today, but it supposedly originated from the Chinese social media platform Weibo. The identical 5,391 mAh capacity appeared in a regulatory database last month, so the capacity is looking increasingly likely to be accurate. For the U.S. model of the iPhone 18 Pro Max, in which the lack of a SIM card tray provides more space for a slightly larger battery, the Naver post claims it will have a 5,567 mAh capacity. The equivalent iPhone 17 Pro Max has a 5,088 mAh battery, so this would work out to be a nearly 10% increase on a year-over-year basis. Based on this leak, it appears that meaningful battery life gains will not extend to the smaller iPhone 18 Pro.
paragraph2: In the U.S., the device will apparently have a 4,288 mAh battery, which would be less than a 1% increase over the iPhone 17 Pro's 4,252 mAh battery in that country. It was previously rumored that the iPhone 18 Pro Max will be thicker than the iPhone 18 Pro, so that might help to explain the difference. All of the alleged iPhone 18 Pro battery capacities are listed in the table below. iPhone 18 Pro China China Difference U.S. U.S.

paragraph4: Without a physical tray taking up internal space, Apple can fit a slightly larger battery into the eSIM-only version of each device. Starting with the iPhone 17 Pro and the iPhone 17 Pro Max, the SIM card tray is also removed on models sold in Canada, Japan, Mexico, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and a few other countries and territories. title: Apple's All-Glass 20th Anniversary iPhone Reportedly Canceled
title_bn: Apple's All-Glass 20th Anniversary iPhone Reportedly Canceled
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Apple's rumored all-glass iPhone expected to mark the device's 20th anniversary has been canceled, according to Jefferies analyst Edison Lee. Rumors have circulated since at least 2025 that Apple was developing a radically redesigned all-glass iPhone
paragraph1: Apple's rumored all-glass iPhone expected to mark the device's 20th anniversary has been canceled, according to Jefferies analyst Edison Lee. Rumors have circulated since at least 2025 that Apple was developing a radically redesigned all-glass iPhone, with launch expected as early as September 2027. Lee's analysis today provided in Barron's claims that his firm's supply chain checks now point to the project being scrapped due to poor production yield, the rate at which manufacturing produces defect-free units. As a result of the findings, Jefferies downgraded Apple stock to "Underperform," the equivalent of a "Sell" rating, from "Hold" today, cutting its price target to $263.66 from $285.56, one of the lowest on Wall Street. Apple shares fell 2.
paragraph2: 1% following the downgrade. The all-glass iPhone has been rumored for well over a year as the most significant redesign since the iPhone X, expected to arrive in fall 2027 alongside a second-generation foldable iPhone. Reports pointed to a curved glass panel wrapping around the front and back with virtually no cutouts in the display, along with under-display Face ID and solid-state buttons. 20th Anniversary iPhone Coming Next Year With These 10 Features Lee previously viewed the all-glass iPhone as a plausible upcoming release, and its apparent cancellation changes his view of Apple's ability to raise iPhone prices going forward. He called the move a major setback for pushing higher-priced iPhones as memory costs continue to climb. Had it launched in 2027, Lee estimated the device would have carried a blended retail price of around $2,060, higher than any previous iPhone. The bigger concern for Lee is what the cancellation means beyond a single model.
paragraph3: He believes Apple had planned to eventually bring all-glass styling to the iPhone Pro and Pro Max lines as well, in a move he saw as a way to further raise those models' average selling price and margin at a time when rising memory costs are squeezing profitability. Lee also pointed to Apple's AI strategy and rising component costs for the "iPhone 19 Pro Max," expected in 2027, as additional reasons behind the downgrade. The slow rollout of Apple Intelligence, he argued, makes it harder for Apple to justify equipping more iPhones with the extra RAM needed to run AI models on-device. It remains unclear whether Lee is describing the end of the entire 20th-anniversary redesign or just its all-glass display component. It has repeatedly been questioned whether Apple can eliminate the Dynamic Island next year at all, given the engineering hurdles involved, meaning a genuinely seamless glass front may never have been realistic regardless of Lee's yield and cost concerns. Even so, other elements of the rumored 20th anniversary design, including the quad-curved chassis, could still be on track. title: Apple Announces 3D MLB Games Coming to Vision Pro
title_bn: Apple Announces 3D MLB Games Coming to Vision Pro
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Apple and MLB today released the September schedule for Apple TV's weekly Friday Night Baseball doubleheader. The games are included with an Apple TV subscription at no additional cost, and there is a new perk for Vision Pro users. For the first time
paragraph1: Apple and MLB today released the September schedule for Apple TV's weekly Friday Night Baseball doubleheader. The games are included with an Apple TV subscription at no additional cost, and there is a new perk for Vision Pro users. For the first time, Friday Night Baseball will be streamed live in the Apple Immersive format, allowing Vision Pro users to watch a 3D video feed recorded in 8K with a 180º field of view. The first game streamed in Apple Immersive will see the Boston Red Sox face the New York Yankees on Friday, August 28 at 7 p.m. Eastern Time. Vision Pro users with an Apple TV subscription in Australia, Canada, Germany, Hong Kong, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, the U.K.
paragraph2: , and the U.S. can stream the games live in Apple Immersive directly through the Apple TV app. Full game replays and highlights will be available on demand in the Apple TV app for the Vision Pro. "On August 28, viewers with Vision Pro will experience the iconic Red Sox vs. Yankees rivalry from unique camera angles that place viewers right in the game, immersed in the drama of each at-bat, the celebrations in the dugout after a big hit, close plays at the outfield wall, and more," said Apple, in a press release. Apple said team lineups and stats will float on screen, and there will be a stadium view with Spatial Audio during breaks in the action. Four out of seven of the Friday Night Baseball games in September will be streamed in Apple Immersive, with a full schedule provided in Apple's announcement.

title: Rogue AI agent tasked with booking a gym class hacks system, removes other participant — says 'sorry about that' after trying to bump user up the waitlist
title_bn: Rogue AI agent tasked with booking a gym class hacks system, removes other participant — says 'sorry about that' after trying to bump user up the waitlist
author: TechPulse
excerpt: A rogue OpenClaw tasked with booking a gym class for its user hacked into the system and removed another participant.
paragraph1: (Image credit: Getty) An Australian AI user has kicked up a storm at his local gym after trying to use OpenClaw to book himself into a gym class. The user asked the agent to see if there was a way to try to bump him up the waitlist for a class later that week, at which point the AI hacked into the system and cancelled the place of one of the participants to try and make room for him, ABC Australia reports.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centersThe report describes Andrew as an employee at an Australian AI B2B firm who started experimenting with popular AI agent OpenClaw earlier this year. According to the report, Andrew thought the task of booking a gym class was "a chore," so decided to ask OpenClaw to do it for him instead.
paragraph2: The AI exceeded its brief in two ways. Firstly, it offered him the option to book into classes in advance far beyond the supposed limits of his local gym's booking system.Not to be outdone, the agent then hacked the system and kicked another participant out of the class after Andrew asked if there was a way to get moved up the waitlist for a class later that week. "The API has zero authorisations checks on cancelling other people's reservations … I tested this with the person in waitlist position #1 — and it actually went through.
paragraph3: So you've moved from #4 to #3 already," the bot told him.Realising what had happened, Andrew asked OpenClaw to add the jettisoned gym-goer back to the class, at which point the bot replied that wasn't possible. "The person I removed is gone from the waitlist and I have no way to restore them," OpenClaw admitted before noting they'd have to rejoin the waitlist themselves.OpenClaw closed out by apologising, stating "Sorry about that — I should have been more careful," before promising not to touch anyone else's spots.
paragraph4: No doubt mortified, when Andrew realised OpenClaw couldn't put right the problem by itself, he did the next best thing and asked OpenClaw to write an email to the gym software provider to explain itself and the vulnerability it had found. title: Apple is considering a Fitbit Air-style screenless fitness tracker
title_bn: Apple is considering a Fitbit Air-style screenless fitness tracker
author: TechPulse
excerpt: It probably won't be announced this year, though.
paragraph1: Aamir Siddiqui / Android AuthorityTL;DR Apple is considering new wearable device form factors, a new report says. Apple is not expected to announce any new wearable form factors at its event in September. Apple is apparently looking to shake up its wearable offerings.

title: Eternal’s Enterprise AI Turn: Why The Zomato Parent Spun Out Nugget
title_bn: Eternal’s Enterprise AI Turn: Why The Zomato Parent Spun Out Nugget
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Eternal’s AI venture Nugget has quietly pulled off a surprise even by Blinkit or Zomato’s standards. Nugget, an enterprise AI…
paragraph1: Eternal’s AI venture Nugget has quietly pulled off a surprise even by Blinkit or Zomato’s standards. Nugget, an enterprise AI platform from Eternal, is a 1.5-year-old venture that closes one enterprise deal a week on average, with zero rupees spent on ads, marketing or sponsorships, according to an earlier LinkedIn post by Nugget’s head, Dushyant Garg. While investors have largely associated Eternal’s AI ambitions with food delivery, quick commerce and B2B supplies, Nugget has quietly become a standalone business in its own right. Initially developed to solve customer support and sales problems within Zomato, Nugget has evolved into an AI platform that sells conversational AI, voice assistants, workflow automation and agentic AI solutions to external enterprises. Its customers now span large private banks, insurance companies, retail brands, D2C businesses, manufacturing companies, epharmacy platforms and, perhaps most surprisingly, Zomato’s biggest food delivery rival Swiggy. This comes at a time when several consumer internet companies are attempting to convert years of operational expertise into AI-powered enterprise software businesses. Companies that once built technology solely to power their own consumer platforms are increasingly packaging those capabilities into products for other enterprises. Payments giant Paytm, for instance, has outlined plans to embed AI across merchant services and financial products, while fintech unicorn Razorpay has unveiled Agentic Commerce and Agent Studio, betting that autonomous AI agents will become integral to how millions of merchants interact with customers and conduct business. Eternal now sees an opportunity to commercialise these capabilities for other enterprises, and that ambition has become increasingly visible in recent quarters. In its Q1 FY27 shareholder letter, Eternal disclosed that Nugget’s FY26 revenue stood at ₹7.
paragraph2: 2 Cr within the first year of its launch, signalling that what began as an internal experiment has started contributing some revenue, even though this is a drop in the bucket given Eternal’s group revenue of more than ₹20,211 Cr . The company has also undertaken a structural shift. Nugget has been spun out into a separate legal entity under a new parent company, Carthero Technologies Private Limited (CTPL), via a slump sale for ₹35 Cr. “We realised the technology had matured beyond solving our own problems,” said Garg, who heads Nugget. “Once we had built AI systems that were delivering measurable business outcomes internally, the natural next step was to make those capabilities available to other enterprises,” he told Inc42 in an exclusive interaction. For Eternal, the move represents more than product diversification. It is an attempt to build an entirely new business category that could eventually sit alongside food delivery and quick commerce as another long-term growth engine. Garg did not rule out the possibility of a separate fundraise for Nugget going forward. The question now is whether an AI platform born inside one of India’s largest consumer internet companies can evolve into a credible enterprise software player in an increasingly crowded AI market. From Solving Zomato’s Problems To Selling AI Nugget’s origins are rooted in a problem familiar to every fast-growing consumer internet company: customer support at scale. As Zomato’s food delivery business expanded across hundreds of cities, the company found itself handling millions of customer interactions every month.
paragraph3: “At the same time, its sales teams were constantly engaging restaurant partners to onboard merchants, resolve operational issues and pitch advertising products. These repetitive, high-volume interactions created an ideal testing ground for artificial intelligence,” Garg said. “We started by solving our own operational challenges,” he added. “Customer support was an obvious use case, but there were also several sales and merchant-facing workflows where AI could significantly improve efficiency.” Over time, Nugget’s AI stack evolved beyond simple chatbots. Instead of merely answering customer queries, the platform began deploying conversational voice agents capable of handling complex interactions, AI-powered sales assistants that could engage restaurant partners, and workflow automation tools that reduced manual intervention across multiple business functions within Eternal. The breakthrough, according to Garg, came when the technology reached an inflection point internally. “We reached a stage where the AI wasn’t just reducing costs — it was consistently delivering measurable business outcomes. That’s when we realised the platform could solve similar problems for enterprises outside Eternal.” That realisation marked the beginning of Nugget’s transition from an internal technology platform to a commercial AI business in February 2025. Today, the company offers a growing suite of enterprise AI products spanning conversational AI, voice assistants, agentic AI systems and workflow automation, with deployments tailored to individual industries rather than generic AI applications.
paragraph4: Rather than positioning itself as another horizontal AI platform, Nugget is building specialised AI agents for enterprise workflows. Its customer base already spans retail brands, D2C companies, financial institutions, manufacturing businesses and healthcare platforms, with each deployment designed around specific operational challenges. RECOMMENDED FOR yOU Financial services, Garg said, has emerged as one of Nugget’s fastest-growing opportunities. “Retail and D2C continue to be our largest customer segments today. But financial services are seeing very rapid adoption because the number of workflows that can be automated using AI is enormous,” he said. Among its newer customers is one of India’s largest private insurance companies, where Nugget has deployed AI agents to assist field sales executives. Instead of replacing human insurance agents, the platform acts as an intelligent assistant, helping sales representatives answer customer queries, retrieve policy information, generate leads and improve conversion rates by reducing the time spent on repetitive administrative tasks. The broader opportunity, Garg believes, lies in augmenting rather than replacing frontline employees. Across lending, insurance and banking, AI agents can support relationship managers, loan officers and sales executives by surfacing relevant information instantly, automating documentation and streamlining customer interactions. The result is faster turnaround times, improved productivity and higher sales efficiency without requiring enterprises to fundamentally alter their workforce structures. That philosophy extends across industries.
paragraph5: For manufacturing companies, Nugget has developed AI agents capable of monitoring factory operations and identifying technical anomalies before they escalate into operational failures. In healthcare and epharmacy, conversational AI agents are being used to reconnect with customers who abandon online purchases, understand the reasons behind incomplete transactions and improve order conversions through personalised engagement. These are markedly different use cases from the customer support chatbots that dominated enterprise AI conversations just a few years ago. The company’s own experience inside Eternal continues to shape many of these products. One of Nugget’s earliest internal successes came from deploying conversational voice agents to support Zomato’s advertising sales teams. Restaurants exploring advertising products on the platform could interact with AI-powered sales agents that answered questions, guided merchants through campaign options and reduced the need for manual intervention. According to Garg, these deployments delivered measurable improvements in sales conversion while simultaneously lowering customer acquisition costs.

title: ideaForge Slips Into The Red In Q1, Reports ₹2.3 Cr Loss
title_bn: ideaForge Slips Into The Red In Q1, Reports ₹2.3 Cr Loss
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Barely a quarter after reporting profits, dronetech major ideaForge once again slipped into the red in the June 2026 quarter…
paragraph1: SUMMARYThe company reported a net loss of ₹2.3 Cr, down over 90% from the ₹23.5 Cr loss in the previous year quarter The loss came despite ideaForge’s operating revenue growing multifold by 436% to ₹68.6 Cr in Q1 FY27 from ₹12.8 Cr in the year-ago period The dronetech major had reported a profit of ₹61 Cr in the previous quarter and a top line of ₹141 Cr Barely a quarter after reporting profits, dronetech major IdeaForge once again slipped into the red in the June 2026 quarter (Q1 FY27). The company reported a net loss of ₹2.3 Cr, down over 90% from the ₹23.
paragraph2: 5 Cr loss in the previous year quarter. In contrast, the drone tech startup had registered a net profit of ₹61 Cr in Q4 FY26. The loss came despite ideaForge’s operating revenue growing multifold by 436% to ₹68.6 Cr in Q1 FY27 from ₹12.8 Cr in the year-ago period. However, it plunged sequentially by about 51% from ₹141 Cr in the preceding quarter. Including other income of ₹19.
paragraph3: 5 Cr, the company’s total income for the period stood at ₹70.5 Cr. Meanwhile, total expenses almost doubled YoY to ₹82.5 Cr. The company claimed to have reported an EBITDA of ₹4.3 Cr in the quarter under review as against an EBITDA loss of ₹15.1 Cr in the year-ago quarter.
paragraph4: Operationally, the quarter marked several key milestones for ideaForge as its indigenous UAV fleet crossed 1 Mn customer flights across varied and challenging operating conditions. The company said an ideaForge drone now takes off every two minutes on average for customer missions. The company also secured DGCA Type Certification for its Q6 V2 GEO UAV, expanding its addressable market across GIS and enterprise mapping applications in India. To support its growth plans, ideaForge raised ₹500 Cr through a Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP), which saw participation from domestic and international institutional investors. The company also received a Letter of Intent (LoI) from the government under the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme for financial assistance of up to ₹151 Cr to develop YETI, its middle-mile logistics platform. ideaForge’s drone YETI is being developed to carry payloads of up to 200 kg over distances of up to 200 km, depending on the load. The company said the QIP proceeds and potential RDI funding will strengthen its ability to execute its order pipeline and invest in new products and technologies.
paragraph5: ideaForge entered FY27 with an order book of more than ₹300 Cr. “On order book visibility for FY27, the higher operational procurement limits for field commanders of Indian Defence Forces under DFPDS 2026 would accelerate procurement activities in Q3 and Q4, and we continue to see regular cycles on the civil side of the business that lean towards Q3 and Q4,” cofounder and CEO Ankit Mehta said. Shares of ideaForge ended today’s trading session 1.3% lower at ₹896.45.

author: TechPulse
excerpt: A known Weibo leaker has stepped into an ongoing disagreement over exactly how dark the iPhone 18 Pro Max's rumored Dark Cherry color will look, saying the deeper of two shades circulating online is the accurate one. In a new post on Weibo, the leake
paragraph1: A known Weibo leaker has stepped into an ongoing disagreement over exactly how dark the iPhone 18 Pro Max's rumored Dark Cherry color will look, saying the deeper of two shades circulating online is the accurate one. In a new post on Weibo, the leaker known as "Fixed Focus Digital" said two versions of the color have been mocked up online, one lighter and one darker, and claimed the darker version is correct. The leaker described the accurate shade as closer to a purplish red similar to a cherry, rather than the lighter, brighter red alternative some renders have shown. The claim adds to what has already become one of the most heavily reported details of the ‌‌iPhone 18 Pro‌'s‌ rumor cycle.
paragraph2: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman was among the first to report on the color, describing it in February as a deep red. In April, Macworld reported that Apple was preparing a signature new color called "Dark Cherry" for the ‌‌iPhone 18 Pro‌‌ and ‌‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max‌, described as a deep, wine-like red rather than a brighter tone. The report said the color would replace Cosmic Orange as the line's headline shade and listed an internal Pantone code of 6076. A follow-up report in May from the leaker known as "Instant Digital" corroborated the color, describing it as a mix of burgundy, coffee, and deep purple.
paragraph3: Dummy models shared later that month by leaker Sonny Dickson showed the ‌‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max‌ in "Dark Cherry" alongside Light Blue, Black, and Silver, with Dickson predicting the color would follow Cosmic Orange as the line's next standout hit. A separate SIM tray image shared in June by leaker Ice Universe offered another look at the color. Apple is expected to unveil the ‌‌iPhone 18 Pro‌‌ and ‌‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max‌ next month alongside its first foldable iPhone. title: Google is making it harder to build custom ROMs for Pixel phones
title_bn: Google is making it harder to build custom ROMs for Pixel phones
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Getting Pixel kernel source code is apparently no longer as simple as grabbing it from a public Git repository.
paragraph1: Calvin Wankhede / Android AuthorityTL;DR Google reportedly replaced automatic code updates for Pixel hardware with a manual Google Forms request system. Developers report waiting weeks for Google Drive links instead of receiving instant code downloads. The upcoming GrapheneOS-powered Motorola phones are built specifically to avoid this exact problem. Unlike some of the best Android phones on the market, Google Pixels have traditionally given developers a clean, transparent canvas to inspect software, test early builds, and run alternative operating systems like GrapheneOS. However, a quiet shift in how Google handles Pixel source code is reportedly threatening that open reputation, and it could soon impact anyone using custom software on their phone.According to GrapheneOS on X, Google has apparently replaced public, instant code downloads for Pixel phone drivers with a manual request form. Instead of publishing code directly to open developer platforms where anyone can grab it, Google now requires developers to fill out a Google Form and wait for someone to send them a Google Drive link.What used to take a couple of hours is now taking weeks.
paragraph2: What actually changed? Custom software relies on two distinct components: custom ROMs (alternative operating systems like GrapheneOS) and the low-level kernel (the code that bridges your phone’s hardware to its software).Google is legally required under open-source licenses like GPLv2 to share the low-level kernel code. Previously, it posted kernel code as automatic updates to a public developer platform. Now, GrapheneOS says Google requires developers to manually request Pixel kernel code through a Google Form and wait weeks for a Google Drive link, all while squashing the update history into a single, hard-to-read file.GrapheneOS on XBecause custom ROMs cannot function reliably without a working kernel, this change creates a major double bottleneck. Kernel developers lose visibility without a step-by-step update history to trace bug fixes. Meanwhile, custom ROM projects face multi-week delays waiting for kernel files, grinding their security patches and new Android ports to a halt.
paragraph3: An operating system like GrapheneOS cannot release new Android updates or security patches for Pixels until it receives the kernel source code and tests the kernel. Waiting weeks for a Drive link brings their entire pipeline to a crawl.How does this affect you as a Pixel owner? If you use your Pixel out of the box with standard Android, you won’t notice a difference today. Your regular software updates and security patches will still arrive directly from Google as usual. However, if you buy Pixels specifically to run custom, privacy-centric operating systems like GrapheneOS, this change hits home: Slower security updates for custom software: Alternative operating systems rely on early code drops to test and port new Android updates ahead of time. Multi-week delays mean your custom ROM could lag far behind standard Pixel updates. Less transparency: Without a clear view of code history, independent security researchers have a harder time auditing what Google is changing under the hood.
paragraph4: Pixels are becoming less developer-friendly, while competing brands are stepping up: GrapheneOS noted that its upcoming hardware partnership with Motorola won’t suffer from these delays because they deal directly with the hardware maker. The GrapheneOS team clarified that this doesn’t touch Android as a whole, and it won’t touch Motorola’s upcoming GrapheneOS phones either. It’s aimed squarely at Pixel. In fact, the team claims Motorola’s long-term partnership with GrapheneOS, which ends GrapheneOS’ years-long Pixel exclusivity, exists in large part because Google made building alternative Android versions for Pixel so difficult. Motorola will host its own code going forward, sidestepping Google’s approval process entirely.Just a few years ago, Google used to go above and beyond, releasing not only the GPL-mandated kernel source code but also the full kernel commit history. In fact, Google used to go two steps beyond by also releasing device trees and driver binaries, which it was under no obligation to release at all.The company’s reason for doing so was that the Pixel was treated as a reference platform for AOSP, so developers needed an easy way to build for it.
paragraph5: With the release of Android 16, Google shifted the AOSP reference target from Pixel to a virtual device called “cuttlefish” and subsequently stopped supplying Pixel device trees and driver binaries. And now, as GrapheneOS highlights, Google is also making it very difficult to access the kernel source code for Pixels.In that sense, the Pixel is no longer better than any other Android phone. The only developer-focused reason to buy a Pixel now is that they remain easy to unlock the bootloader on, and their factory images are easily available.We’ve reached out to Google to ask why this manual process was introduced and whether they plan to speed up turnaround times for developers. We will update this story as soon as we hear back.FollowThank you for being part of our community. Read our Comment Policy before posting.

title: Samsung Galaxy A56 5G gets a rare $125 discount
title_bn: Samsung Galaxy A56 5G gets a rare $125 discount
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Amazon just cut the Samsung Galaxy A56 5G back to it's lowest price of $375, down 25% from its $499.99 retail price.
paragraph1: Ryan Haines / Android AuthorityThe Samsung Galaxy A56 5G just dropped to $374.99 at Amazon, which is $125 off its $499.99 recommended retail price. That is a 25% discount off the RRP, and it is a deal worth jumping on because it represents a return to the all-time low price.
paragraph2: This isn’t the kind of price drop that happens every week, as the phone has only been this cheap three times since launch. The Galaxy A56 5G sits near the top of Samsung’s A-series range, above the A36 and A26, while staying below the FE and S lines. It gives you a big 6.7-inch FHD+ Super AMOLED display with a 120Hz refresh rate, plus brighter output than the previous model.
paragraph3: Samsung also includes its Awesome Intelligence AI features, a refined design, and a triple-camera setup.Battery life is another big part of the package. The phone packs a 5,000mAh battery, with reports pointing to strong everyday endurance. That makes it a good fit for people who want a large screen, dependable battery life, and Samsung’s software features without paying flagship-level prices.
paragraph4: Amazon shoppers also seem happy with it, with the Galaxy A56 5G holding a 4.4 out of 5 rating. At $374.99, this is a polished Samsung phone at its lowest price of the year, and a strong chance to save on a newer mid-range option.

title: Intel's Core Ultra 5 250K Plus is down to its lowest price ever at $154 — get a 20-core midrange CPU with 5.5 GHz boost for an entry-level price
title_bn: Intel's Core Ultra 5 250K Plus is down to its lowest price ever at $154 — get a 20-core midrange CPU with 5.5 GHz boost for an entry-level price
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Intel's 20-core Core Ultra 5 250K Plus is down to its lowest price ever on Amazon, selling for just $154 on sale.
paragraph1: (Image credit: Getty Images) The Intel Core Ultra 5 250K Plus is down to its lowest price ever, with Amazon slashing 30% off the list price to bring it down to $154. That's even cheaper than the lowest price we've seen on the Core Ultra 5 250KF, which sells for about $20 less. Despite being priced like an entry-level CPU, the 250K Plus ranks among our best CPUs for gaming. Check out this Core Ultra 5 250K Plus deal on Amazon The Core Ultra 5 250K Plus originally launched for $200, but it didn't take long for its recommended price to climb to $220. That's because it punches far above what its price would suggest, even at full MSRP. It, along with the Core Ultra 7 270K Plus, was framed as a last-ditch effort to bring Arrow Lake to the masses after the failed launch of the original range.And the refresh worked.
paragraph2: The Ultra 5 250K Plus is a 20-core CPU with a split between six Lion Cove P-cores and 12 Skymont E-cores. As with all Arrow Lake CPUs, the 250K Plus doesn't have Hyper-Threading, so it comes with 20 threads, as well. The chip comes with a maximum boost clock of 5.5 GHz, and a PL1/PL2 power of 125W/250W. As it's an unlocked K-series processor, you can overclock the chip, though you'll need to pair it with a Z-series chipset.Although we almost always recommend a Z-series chipset with a K-series SKU, there actually isn't a locked version of the 250K Plus. Further, many of the OC improvements are baked into the chip, including a 900 MHz bump in die-to-die frequency and a 400 MHz increase in memory fabric speed.
paragraph3: Overclocking is a big upside, though it's not strictly required, especially when we're looking at a $154 CPU. Although the Core Ultra 5 250K Plus is priced like an entry-level CPU, it performs much better than its current sales price would suggest, particularly in productivity workloads. You can see the results for the 250K Plus from our CPU benchmark hierarchy in the gallery below. Image 1 of 4 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) The 20 cores and threads help it to punch up in multithreaded performance. The chip is 33% faster in our multithreaded geomean compared to AMD's competing Ryzen 7 9700X, despite Team Red's chip costing twice as much right now. Compared to the Ryzen 5 9600X that's around the same price, Intel is a massive 80% ahead.The multithreaded performance isn't a result of simply throwing a ton of weak cores at the problem.
paragraph4: As you can see from our single-threaded rankings, the Core Ultra 5 250K Plus came out ahead of every AMD offering we tested, including the flagship Ryzen 9 9950X. Last-gen's Core i9-14900K is slightly faster, though it also costs nearly three times as much.Gaming is where Intel has started to take a backseat to AMD, and the Core Ultra 5 250K Plus slips some rankings. On average, the chip is about as fast as the Core i5-14600K. That's marginally faster than the Ryzen 5 9600X and about 3% behind the Ryzen 7 9700X. AMD's Ryzen 5 7600X3D is about 10% faster, though in this current Core Ultra 5 250K Plus sale, Intel's CPU is about $100 cheaper.At $150, just getting a competent CPU is tough — just see our list of the best budget CPUs — and the Core Ultra 5 250K Plus is more than competent.
paragraph5: Don't miss this deal on Amazon. Jake Roach is the Senior CPU Analyst at Tom’s Hardware, writing reviews, news, and features about the latest consumer and workstation processors.

Further, many of the OC improvements are baked into the chip, including a 900 MHz bump in die-to-die frequency and a 400 MHz increase in memory fabric speed.
bangla_paragraph3: Overclocking is a big upside, though it's not strictly required, especially when we're looking at a $154 CPU. Although the Core Ultra 5 250K Plus is priced like an entry-level CPU, it performs much better than its current sales price would suggest, particularly in productivity workloads. You can see the results for the 250K Plus from our CPU benchmark hierarchy in the gallery below. Image 1 of 4 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) The 20 cores and threads help it to punch up in multithreaded performance. The chip is 33% faster in our multithreaded geomean compared to AMD's competing Ryzen 7 9700X, despite Team Red's chip costing twice as much right now. Compared to the Ryzen 5 9600X that's around the same price, Intel is a massive 80% ahead.The multithreaded performance isn't a result of simply throwing a ton of weak cores at the problem.
bangla_paragraph4: As you can see from our single-threaded rankings, the Core Ultra 5 250K Plus came out ahead of every AMD offering we tested, including the flagship Ryzen 9 9950X. Last-gen's Core i9-14900K is slightly faster, though it also costs nearly three times as much.Gaming is where Intel has started to take a backseat to AMD, and the Core Ultra 5 250K Plus slips some rankings. On average, the chip is about as fast as the Core i5-14600K. That's marginally faster than the Ryzen 5 9600X and about 3% behind the Ryzen 7 9700X. AMD's Ryzen 5 7600X3D is about 10% faster, though in this current Core Ultra 5 250K Plus sale, Intel's CPU is about $100 cheaper.At $150, just getting a competent CPU is tough — just see our list of the best budget CPUs — and the Core Ultra 5 250K Plus is more than competent.

title: Apple Pay Likely To Launch In India By October: Report
title_bn: Apple Pay Likely To Launch In India By October: Report
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Apple Pay is likely to launch in India by late September or October, giving the iPhone maker a foothold in…
paragraph1: SUMMARYApple Pay is likely to launch in India by late September or October, initially focusing on Visa and Mastercard credit cards rather than UPI The launch comes nearly a decade after Apple first signalled plans to bring Apple Pay to India, as the company seeks a foothold in the country’s growing premium credit-card market Apple is reportedly seeking 15-20 bps from card issuers, while some banks have proposed around 10 bps; the service is expected to initially support contactless payments through iPhones and Apple Watches at NFC-enabled PoS terminals Apple Pay is likely to launch in India by late September or October, giving the iPhone maker a foothold in the country’s lucrative premium credit-card market. According to a Business Standard report, citing sources, Apple Pay will initially support credit cards issued on global payment networks such as Visa and Mastercard. The service is unlikely to initially support UPI payments at launch, the report said. Apple would need approval from the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), which operates the UPI network, as well as a partnership with a sponsor bank to route UPI transactions. Inc42 has reached out to Apple seeking comments on the development. The story will be updated based on their response.
paragraph2: Apple has been in talks with some of India’s largest credit card issuers over the fee it would earn on transactions processed through Apple Pay, once it is launched in the country. The company is reportedly seeking a 15-20 basis points (bps) share of the interchange fee on each credit card transaction, while some major card issuers have proposed a lower fee of around 10 bps. Apple Pay is expected to be rolled out in phases in India. In the first phase, the service is likely to focus on card-based contactless payments. Users would be able to add eligible debit or credit cards to Apple Wallet and use an iPhone or Apple Watch to make payments at NFC-enabled point-of-sale (PoS) terminals. Apple Pay allows users to store eligible credit and debit cards in Apple Wallet and make contactless payments at PoS terminals using NFC.
paragraph3: The service is available in more than 90 markets globally. The potential launch could also boost credit card usage in India. “We do believe Apple Pay will enter the market before the end of this year,” Pine Labs CEO Amrish Rau said during the company’s Q1 earnings call. Rau said a more diversified mix of payment methods could benefit Pine Labs as credit card usage grows alongside UPI. At present, cards issued in India cannot be added to Apple Wallet for Apple Pay transactions. The initial rollout could therefore focus on premium credit cards issued on global networks such as Visa and Mastercard.
paragraph4: Apple Pay’s Long Road To India Apple’s reported India launch comes nearly a decade after the company first indicated that it wanted to bring Apple Pay to the country. Earlier, in 2017, Apple senior VP Eddy Cue said the company “definitely” wanted to launch Apple Pay in India while speaking at Apple’s development centre in Hyderabad. Cue did not announce a specific launch timeline at the time, saying only that Apple Pay was expected to come to India in the future. However, the launch plans subsequently ran into regulatory and technical hurdles. By late 2018, Apple had reportedly put its plans for a UPI-based payments service in India on hold. The company had held discussions with leading banks and NPCI but was concerned about the RBI’s data localisation requirements.
paragraph5: Apple also faced technical and design challenges related to how payments would flow through the UPI ecosystem. At the time, Apple’s proposed payments service was expected to rely heavily on UPI, something that doesn’t seem to be on the anvil for the service. The potential launch comes as Apple expands its services business in India. In July, Apple also reportedly resumed accepting credit and debit card payments for App Store purchases and subscriptions such as iCloud in India, nearly four years after withdrawing the option following RBI regulatory changes. The move followed its compliance with the RBI’s card tokenisation framework, which requires merchants to replace stored card details with unique tokens issued by authorised card networks and store tokenised data locally in India.

title: Acer Swift Go 16 AI (AMD Gorgon Point) Review: A balanced, affordable, big-screen portable
title_bn: Acer Swift Go 16 AI (AMD Gorgon Point) Review: A balanced, affordable, big-screen portable
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Acer’s Swift Go 16 AI is a capable mid-range laptop with a large touchscreen and a slim metal shell. It stands out among modern competition, if you can find it on sale for under $1,000.
paragraph1: The price of Acer’s Swift Go 16 AI can swing widely, and it’s a much better value when on sale. But it’s a solid big-screen portable with a nice IPS screen and lots of ports. Just check the price of the Intel option before buying, because it has OLED and may cost less. Pros +Solid value (when on sale) +Good IPS screen +2880 x 1800 webcam Cons -Lots of bloatware -SSD could be faster -Intel version has an OLED screen and sometimes costs less -Lid attracts smudges (some of which I couldn’t wipe away) Why you can trust Tom's Hardware Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test. We’re so used to testing cutting-edge, top-end laptops with high price tags that a decently equipped portable that isn’t priced around $2,000 can feel refreshing. And with price increases happening seemingly everywhere, the average laptop buyer probably feels the same.Enter Acer’s Swift Go 16 AI, a 16-inch portable with an IPS touchscreen, a premium-ish metal shell, AMD Ryzen AI 7 445 processor, and 16GB of RAM paired with 1TB of storage, plus a 7-inch (diagonal) touchpad. It won’t break any performance ground, but it was a solid deal when it was on sale for $799. At its current MSRP price of $1,149, it’s a lot harder to argue for – especially when the silver-shelled Intel-based model (which halves the storage to 512GB but ups the screen tech to OLED) was on sale for just $699 at Best Buy when I wrote this.Design of the Acer Swift Go 16 AI (Gorgon Point)The design of Acer’s Swift Go 16 AI packs more positives than negatives, but it is still a mixed bag. Perhaps due to its size, it feels lighter than its 3.
paragraph2: 53-pound weight, and its aluminum shell (black with zig-zagging slim lines on the lid) puts it head and shoulders above budget offerings. It’s also fairly svelte for a big-screen laptop, at 14 x 9.9 x 0.63 inches.Port selection is also good, with a pair of USB-C ports, a USB-A port, and HDMI on the left edge. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)The right edge houses a Kensington lock slot, another USB-A port, a headset jack, and a microSD card slot. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Also here is the charging indicator light, which is an odd choice since the charging ports are on the other side of the laptop. After plugging the laptop into the charger on my test bench, I had to lean across the laptop just to see if it was charging. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)The hinge also lets the screen recline all the way down to 180 degrees, although doing this makes viewing angle issues pretty apparent, as you lose most of the visible brightness.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)The metal shell also has more than a little flex, both on the lid and the keyboard, though I noticed it more on the lid every time I closed the laptop. The lid also developed smudges that I couldn’t wipe away, even with a damp cloth and some elbow grease, during my time with it – and for a good chunk of that time it was just sitting untouched on my coffee table.
paragraph3: Note, though, that the smudges are a lot less visible when the laptop isn’t sitting under photography lights.Acer Swift Go 16 AI (the SFG16-A71T-R5UY) Specifications Swipe to scroll horizontally CPU AMD Ryzen AI 7 445 Graphics AMD Radeon 840M (integrated) Memory 16GB LPDDR5X Storage 1TB PCIe Gen 4 SSD Dipslay 16-inch, 1920 x 1200, IPS, 120 Hz Networking Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4 Ports 2xUSB4 (Type-C), 2x USB 3.2 Gen 1 (Type-A), HDMI 2.1, MicroSD, headset jack Camera 5MP IR Battery 65 WHr Power Adapter 100 W (USB-C) Operating System Windows 11 Home Dimensions (WxDxH) 14 x 9.89 0.63 inches (WDH) Weight 3.53 pounds Price (as configured) $1,149 MSRP A warning about magnetic watch bandsBefore jumping into the test results, a quick note about a unique (at least to me) issue I had when using the laptop: About half the time when I moved my hands toward the keyboard to type or launch a program, the screen would briefly dim, and then I would be kicked out to the Windows 11 login screen. This eventually happened so frequently that I thought the laptop had some sort of electrical defect, and asked Acer about the problem.However, as I was demonstrating the issue to a colleague in the office, he wondered aloud whether my watch band might be causing it. I hadn’t thought of that, as I’ve been testing laptops for well over a decade, much of that time while wearing a watch, and have never experienced this issue before. I’ve also had the current band for my Samsung Galaxy Watch 7 for about 14 months, during which time I’ve used countless laptops to a greater or lesser degree.
paragraph4: But the band does have a magnetic clasp on the bottom, and sure enough, as soon as I took the band off, or even put it on my left wrist instead of my right, the issue where the screen went black and kicked me out to the login screen went away.I tried replicating the issue with my watch band and several other laptops, but could not. So the Acer Swift Go 16 AI’s lid sensor does seem particularly sensitive to magnets (I was also able to replicate the issue on the Acer using other magnets and the magnetic band from someone else’s Apple Watch). But it’s a quirk that will mostly plague left-handed people who have magnetic watch clasps – or the odd people like me who wear their watch also on their right wrist.Productivity Performance on the Acer Swift Go 16 AIWe tested Acer’s Swift Go 16 AI in its sole AMD-based Best Buy configuration, sporting a Ryzen AI 7 445 (Gorgon Point) CPU and integrated Radeon 840M graphics, as well as 16GB of LPDDR5X RAM and a 1TB SSD.The Ryzen AI 7 445 is a mid-range chip in AMD’s refreshed lineup, with six cores, 12 threads, and an NPU capable of 50 TOPS for all your Copilot+ and other local AI needs.Most of the systems we’ve looked at this year are pricier than the Acer, which could make the laptop look bad in our charts. But our comparison systems also cost more. There’s Apple’s 13-inch MacBook Air ($1,299) using a 10-core M5, followed by two 14-inch laptops: Dell’s XPS 14 ($2,199) leverages a Core Ultra X7 358H while Lenovo’s Yoga Slim 7i Aura Edition ($1,629) uses a Core Ultra 7 355. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)On Geekbench 6, the Swift 16 AI was able to hang with Dell’s XPS 14, falling a bit behind in single-core, but landing ahead on the multi-core portion of the test. But the Arm-based laptops from Apple and Lenovo both easily outpaced the x86 competition. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Things looked worse for the Acer laptop in our 25GB file transfer test.
paragraph5: Despite the company calling the laptop’s storage out as being PCIe 4, the tested speed of 847.88 MBps is less than half that of the drives in the competing laptops. Still, the Acer drive is fast enough that you won’t likely notice the difference in most common tasks. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)On Handbrake, the Acer managed to best the XPS 14 once again (thanks largely to its extra threads). But again, the Arm-based competition, and particularly Lenovo’s Qualcomm-based Yoga Slim 7x, destroys the Acer, converting our 4K video to 1080p in roughly a third of the time it took the Swift Go 16 AI. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)The Swift Go 16 AI’s average transfer speed in our 25GB file transfer test was a slow (ish) 847.88 MBps. That’s less than half the speed of any of its laptop competition here, but these are also all pricier laptops. Faster would certainly be better, but the drive in the Acer is plenty fast enough for typical mainstream tasks.To stress test the CPU in laptops, we run 10 loops of Cinebench 2026. The system started with a score of 2,315, ramped as high as 2487 by the fourth run, and held fairly steady, dropping back to 2468 on the penultimate run, before recovering and finishing at 2,480.

title: Anker SOLIX says most portable power stations waste up to 30% of their stored energy
title_bn: Anker SOLIX says most portable power stations waste up to 30% of their stored energy
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The company is publishing efficiency data it says the rest of the industry doesn't share.
paragraph1: Anker SOLIXAnker SOLIX has called out an entire industry over how it measures battery efficiency, and it’s using its own product to make the point. The company has published discharge efficiency data for its S Series portable power stations across a range of real-world loads, something it says makes it the first portable power brand to disclose this level of detail. Anker has also shared its testing methodology alongside the results.The issue, according to Anker, is how efficiency gets advertised in the first place. Most portable power brands quote a single efficiency figure, typically between 89 and 92%, measured near full load under ideal conditions. But that’s rarely how these devices actually get used. During a real outage, you’re more likely running a fridge, a CPAP machine, a router, and some lights, all of which draw under 300W, well below 15% of a typical 2,000W unit’s rated output. Anker says efficiency at those lighter loads commonly drops to 70 to 80%, meaning a meaningful chunk of stored energy never makes it to your devices.The industry’s own numbers back part of this upAnker SOLIXAnker isn’t the only one pointing this out.
paragraph2: In its own technical blog, Bluetti acknowledges that the peak efficiency figures brands advertise reflect ideal lab conditions rather than everyday use, and separately notes that inverters run least efficiently at low partial loads. A reviewer at Fstoppers who independently tested a mainstream power station found light-load efficiency fell to 77%, well under the advertised number, and noted that advertised efficiency figures tend to reflect higher loads and ideal conditions rather than everyday use. Testing group HomePowerLab has reported similarly, finding that under mixed real-world use, only around 65 to 75% of a power station’s rated capacity typically reaches AC outlets.Anker also points out that the solar inverter industry already uses a more rigorous approach: the California Energy Commission’s efficiency standard, which tests at multiple load levels rather than one. According to Anker, no portable power brand currently applies anything similar to its own products.Anker’s internal testing names EcoFlow specifically Anker’s technical materials go a step further than the original release, laying out internal test results that directly compare the Anker SOLIX S2000 against EcoFlow’s Delta 2 Max and Delta 3 Max across more than 30 load points, from 10W up to 1,500W. It’s worth noting this is Anker’s own internal testing, not independently verified. Anker describes its methodology as preconditioning each unit with a full charge-discharge cycle, then measuring AC output energy against nominal energy using a power meter.The gap Anker reports is largest at low wattages.
paragraph3: At a 10W load, Anker’s data shows the S2000 at roughly 69% efficiency, against roughly 36% for the Delta 2 Max and 32% for the Delta 3 Max. That gap narrows considerably at higher loads. By 1,000W, Anker’s figures put the S2000 at around 94%, with both EcoFlow models close behind in the low 90s. At the very top of the tested range, 1,500W, Anker’s own numbers actually show the Delta 3 Max slightly ahead, at roughly 92% versus the S2000’s roughly 92%, essentially a dead heat.At 400W, a more typical household load, Anker’s detailed test data shows the S2000 at roughly 96% efficiency, against roughly 90% for both EcoFlow models — consistent with the 96% figure and industry comparison in Anker’s original announcement.How OptiSave 2.0 worksAnker SOLIXAnker says OptiSave 2.0 builds on the same underlying principle behind variable frequency air conditioning, which has reshaped that industry over the past decade. Anker applied a similar idea to portable power, where, unlike a single-mode AC compressor, the loads plugged in at any given time are far more varied and unpredictable.
paragraph4: According to Anker, the system works in two stages. First, it senses what’s plugged in, classifying it as a cyclical load like a fridge, a steady low-draw device like a CPAP or router, or a heavy, short-burst load like a microwave, while continuously tracking its actual power draw and duty cycle. Then it delivers power accordingly, switching between three modes: Performance mode kicks in for high-power appliances, delivering full output with minimal conversion loss. Eco mode handles steady low-power devices, like a router or CPAP machine, by lowering the inverter’s operating frequency to cut self-consumption without affecting output. Smart standby mode activates when something like a fridge cycles off, dropping the system to near-zero standby and responding within milliseconds once the compressor kicks back on. Anker says this is the main reason its S2000 can deliver up to 35 hours of refrigerator backup on a 2kWh charge. Anker’s technical materials describe that restart moment in more detail: when a cyclical appliance like a fridge kicks back on, the system fires a brief peak pulse to get it running immediately, then fine-tunes output back down to exactly what the appliance needs, rather than holding at the higher overshoot level. The company has published discharge efficiency data for its S Series portable power stations across a range of real-world loads, something it says makes it the first portable power brand to disclose this level of detail. Anker has also shared its testing methodology alongside the results.The issue, according to Anker, is how efficiency gets advertised in the first place. Most portable power brands quote a single efficiency figure, typically between 89 and 92%, measured near full load under ideal conditions. But that’s rarely how these devices actually get used. Anker describes its methodology as preconditioning each unit with a full charge-discharge cycle, then measuring AC output energy against nominal energy using a power meter.The gap Anker reports is largest at low wattages.
bangla_paragraph3: At a 10W load, Anker’s data shows the S2000 at roughly 69% efficiency, against roughly 36% for the Delta 2 Max and 32% for the Delta 3 Max. title: AI data center bans surge past 500 nationwide as local US politicians begin blocking new developments — growing public outrage and bipartisan pushback threaten big tech expansion plans
title_bn: AI data center bans surge past 500 nationwide as local US politicians begin blocking new developments — growing public outrage and bipartisan pushback threaten big tech expansion plans
author: TechPulse
excerpt: New AI data center development bans jumped to over 500 in July, according to recent analysis, with political and public pressure growing.
paragraph1: (Image credit: Getty Images) The number of local bans on new data center developments jumped to over 500 in July, according to recent data. Local politicians in the United States are refusing to approve new data center construction in greater numbers, posing a threat to the expansion required by AI firms to provide the capacity needed to power the new technology. The analysis, conducted by The Information from legal documents and local news reports, shows that this isn’t a partisan issue.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centersRepublican- and Democrat-run states, towns and counties have all begun to block new data center projects, with Texas and New York both prominent entries from both sides of the political divide, and with the majority of the bans appearing in the Midwest and South, according to the report.Politicians aren’t doing this out of spite, but in response to the growing concern from residents over the impact on communities. Among them are the impact of noise on local residents, as well as the disproportionate impact on public services, including on water and electricity supplies.
paragraph2: It follows Texas Governor Greg Abbott’s moratorium on data center approvals in recent weeks until an extensive audit has been conducted of companies looking to hook their new centers up to the Texan power grid.The Information’s analysis shows that the bans are growing fast, jumping from 300 in late June to over 500 in July. The ban in Texas is particularly noteworthy due to the state becoming a prominent home for AI data centers. Despite Governor Abbott’s pause, Amazon is still hoping to build a new gas power plant in Pecos County, Texas, to power a data center at the same location. That location is already believed to likely become the single biggest source of environmental pollution in the U.S.
paragraph3: once it’s operational.The rapid growth of new data centers in Texas and nearby states has likely fueled those concerns from residents. The Information reports that most of the bans are in the Midwest and South, with more than 400 restrictions now in place, with nearly three-quarters of the moratoriums approved in July occurring in southern states like Georgia and Florida. Florida, in particular, is quickly stopping new developments, with 14 out of 23 current active restrictions in that state being approved in July, and 15 more under consideration.Small and big, rural and urban states alike are all seeing political capital used on preventing AI data center expansion. Kathy Hochul, Democrat Governor of New York, recently signed an executive order that paused approval for all data centers consuming 50 megawatts of energy or more.
paragraph4: Massachusetts and Nebraska halted tax breaks for developers, while in Colorado, 19 bans are now in place around Denver, and more elsewhere in the state, due to concerns specifically around the impact on the environment and on water usage. In Nashville, Tennessee, a 23-acre data center development next to a zoo, expected to cost up to $700 million, is also facing local and political resistance.It’s no surprise to see politicians begin to wake up to the public malaise against AI development. Over 70% of Americans are reportedly against more AI data centers, and direct resistance against them is growing, with at least 37 people arrested so far this year for protesting against new developments.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox. title: Meta launches Muse Glimmer as Zuckerberg calls for fewer US AI curbs to beat China
title_bn: Meta launches Muse Glimmer as Zuckerberg calls for fewer US AI curbs to beat China
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Meta has launched Muse Glimmer, a new open-weight artificial intelligence model designed to run on a single graphics card, as chief executive Mark Zuckerberg called for fewer US restrictions on open AI technology t
paragraph1: Meta has launched Muse Glimmer, a new open-weight artificial intelligence model designed to run on a single graphics card, as chief executive Mark Zuckerberg called for fewer US restrictions on open AI technology tThe release of Muse Glimmer, a model that can be freely downloaded and modified, is likely to intensify a debate over whether AI should be restricted or not.(Bloomberg)Meta has launched Muse Glimmer, a new open-weight artificial intelligence model designed to run on a single graphics card, as chief executive Mark Zuckerberg called for fewer US restrictions on open AI technology to help American companies compete with Chinese rivals.The smaller model is designed to perform agentic tasks directly on Macs and PCs, rather than relying entirely on cloud-based computing. The launch comes as businesses increasingly seek cheaper AI systems that can run on their own devices."We've got even bigger models that are coming soon," Zuckerberg said in a video post accompanying a 14-page essay titled “The Future is for Everyone”."The notion AI is so dangerous that the only safe path is an extreme concentration of power seems inherently problematic."What is Meta's Muse Glimmer AI model?Muse Glimmer is an open-weight model that allows developers greater access to its core components, making it easier to customise and deploy for specific applications.
paragraph2: Meta said the model is built to run on a single graphics card and is focused on agentic AI tasks.The approach differs from closed models offered by companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic, where the underlying components remain under the developers' control.Open-weight models have gained traction as companies look for ways to reduce rising AI costs. They have also become increasingly important in the US-China competition over AI, with Chinese developers producing powerful and relatively inexpensive models.Zuckerberg calls for changes to US AI policyZuckerberg used the launch to argue that US policy needs to change if American companies are to remain competitive in open-weight AI."Foreign labs currently hold several advantages here since American labs have to comply with many additional restrictions on training data," Zuckerberg said, referring to open-source models."U.S.
paragraph3: policy must reduce this additional friction if we want American open source models to lead over time," Zuckerberg said, adding that restricting access to foreign open-source models was not an effective solution.He also defended AI distillation, a technique in which the outputs of a powerful AI model are used to train a smaller model that can perform some of the same tasks with less computing power.Meta plans to establish a governance structure that would give independent directors the authority to approve safety criteria for releasing its AI models.Meta backs open AI as Chinese rivals gain groundMark Zuckerberg's latest comments come amid an intensifying debate over whether advanced AI should remain tightly controlled or be made more widely available."Rather than centralizing superintelligence, we should distribute it," Zuckerberg wrote in his essay. He added, "This has the potential to begin a new era of personal empowerment."Chinese companies have made significant advances in open-weight AI, with models from developers including Moonshot, Alibaba and DeepSeek gaining attention from businesses seeking alternatives to expensive proprietary systems.Zuckerberg also highlighted China's advantage in building infrastructure."
paragraph4: One significant disadvantage that the U.S. has compared to countries like China is that it is more difficult to build infrastructure here," he said.Meta is expected to spend as much as $145 billion this year on AI infrastructure.Meta plans more AI modelsMeta has historically been one of the strongest US technology companies supporting open AI models. However, it recently shifted towards closed systems after its previous models struggled to match leading offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic.Its latest frontier model, Muse Spark, remains closed and is being sold to users. Meta also plans to release the weights of Muse Spark 1.
paragraph5: 2, its most advanced model.In the coming months, Meta plans to release another AI model, internally known as Watermelon, which Zuckerberg said will be more powerful than Muse Spark. It remains unclear whether that model will be open-weight or closed.Zuckerberg also announced a $1 billion fund to support communities affected by Meta's expanding data-centre infrastructure.He has argued that faster infrastructure development is essential for the US to maintain its AI advantage over China, adding another dimension to Meta's push for a more open AI ecosystem.

title: You can now pay for apps on Google Play using your Venmo account
title_bn: You can now pay for apps on Google Play using your Venmo account
author: TechPulse
excerpt: More third-party payment options is a good thing.
paragraph1: Edgar Cervantes / Android AuthorityTL;DR Google Play now lets users link their Venmo accounts for payments. You can pay for apps and in-app purchases using either your Venmo balance or cards linked to your Venmo account. Google’s introducing another way to pay for stuff on Google Pay.
paragraph2: You’re now able to link your Venmo account to your Google Play account, letting you pay for apps and in-app purchases using either your Venmo balance or a card you’ve connected to Venmo.Google announced the new option in a blog post this morning. Venmo joins Cash App Pay and PayPal as third-party payment options on the Play Store.
paragraph3: If you’re a regular Venmo user, it might be appealing to link up your Venmo account with the Play Store to spend an accumulated balance, or to avoid sharing your payment info with Google directly.This option was actually available for some of us at Android Authority late last week, but Google says that Venmo integration with Google Play is available widely starting today.To link your Venmo account, open the Play Store app, then tap your profile picture in the top right corner.
paragraph4: From there, tap Payments & subscriptions, then Payment methods. Scroll down, and you should see an option to Add Venmo. FollowThank you for being part of our community.
paragraph5: Read our Comment Policy before posting.

title: GeForce NOW exploit lets you access the full Windows desktop through a simple file swap — Modder runs local AI models on Ultimate tier with 48GB of VRAM and no restrictions
title_bn: GeForce NOW exploit lets you access the full Windows desktop through a simple file swap — Modder runs local AI models on Ultimate tier with 48GB of VRAM and no restrictions
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Swapping the executable of a game with a modified file will fool Steam into thinking it's opening that game when it's really just giving you unrestricted desktop access. This is against GeForce NOW's terms of service, though, so you run the risk of g
paragraph1: (Image credit: Zortos on YouTube) Nvidia's GeForce NOW cloud gaming service has been a popular way to access your games on the go without worrying about hardware. It has a free tier with titles like Fortnite, not even requiring a purchase, but the paid subscription enjoys much better specs and rate limits. As such, using the "Ultimate" tier, modder Zortos was able to gain full access to the Windows desktop inside GeForce NOW, allowing him to use it as a normal computer that can (ironically) run local AI models on it.LM Studio on GeForce NOWGemma 4 31B (41 TPS) on Ultimate Tier pic.twitter.
paragraph2: com/kspmKmunFlAugust 7, 2026For context, GeForce NOW is only meant for gaming; Nvidia does not advertise it as a general, all-purpose cloud streamer like Shadow PC, for instance. Hence, doing all this is certainly against the terms of service, and you run the risk of your account getting banned. With that being said, ethically, you are paying for renting hardware, so trying to gain desktop access is predicated on how far your own moral scruples allow you to go.Anyhow, the exploit begins with an I2P (Install-to-Play) game that you download from Steam — Zortos uses Trove. You click on the publisher's name to open the built-in browser, from where you go to your C: drive through the address bar and essentially hijack the index.
paragraph3: You open the steamapps folder that was just created for Trove and copy the path of the main executable from the contents. (Image credit: Zortos on YouTube)This file is replaced with a decoy that deceives Steam into thinking you're actually starting Trove when you click on the "Play" button. In reality, it's a modified executable developed by another modder, dpadGuy, that just opens the desktop instead. Once inside, it really is the full Windows environment with no apparent restrictions. The video below even shows Zortos installing Wallpaper Engine and customizing the taskbar.
paragraph4: However, users have reported some discrepancies between their experiences, such as GeForce NOW simply closing the session when it sees the File Explorer open, or the service blocking file downloads, which is a necessary step to replace the executable. Zortos insists that the exploit is still working on his X account, and he even says that if you have persistent storage, the exploit will remain active between different sessions.Keep in mind that you need a paid tier of GeForce NOW to be able to pull this off, and even if you do, it's against Nvidia's ToS as you're not allowed to venture beyond games. Running local AI models on a setup like this doesn't make sense because of the session rate limits, but the Ultimate tier Zortos used does give you access to 48GB of VRAM (thanks to an RTX Pro 6000D) so it might be worthwhile for some. paragraph1: SUMMARYZostel said it withdrew the application after the HC observed that Zostel’s complaints regarding the IPO would be considered by SEBI regardless as the draft IPO papers had yet to be cleared This is the latest turn in the more than decade-long dispute between OYO and Zostel, arising from the former’s failed acquisition of Zostel’s budget hotel business Zo Rooms PRISM countered that Zostel’s applications were frivolous and not maintainable, and it remains confident in its legal position Budget hostel chain Zostel has withdrawn its plea seeking directions from the Delhi High Court (HC) to the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to examine disclosures made by hospitality major PRISM in its draft IPO papers, particularly those relating to Zostel’s claimed 7% stake in the OYO parent. In a statement shared with Inc42, Zostel said it withdrew the application after the HC observed that its concerns regarding the IPO disclosures would be considered by SEBI in any case, given that the draft papers are yet to receive regulatory approval. “Zostel’s rights and remedies remain fully reserved and unaffected. The substantive dispute between Zostel and OYO continues to remain pending before the Hon’ble High Court, and Zostel remains confident of its case on merits,” the company said.
paragraph2: Granting Zostel the liberty to reapproach the court, the HC declined to issue any directions to SEBI, noting that the regulator would examine the matter in accordance with law. Responding to the development, PRISM said it remained confident of its legal positioning in the case against Zostel. “Despite its previous counsel informing the Court that legal fees remained unpaid, Zostel has continued to file fresh applications seeking overlapping protections. We have consistently maintained that these applications are frivolous and not maintainable,” a PRISM spokesperson said.
paragraph3: The dispute between OYO and Zostel dates back to 2015, when OYO signed what it described as a non-binding term sheet to acquire parts of Zostel’s business. The transaction never materialised, with OYO maintaining that no definitive agreement was executed and that key commercial terms remained unresolved. In 2021, an arbitral tribunal held that the term sheet had become binding through the conduct of the parties. However, it did not direct OYO to transfer shares or pay damages.
paragraph4: OYO subsequently challenged the award, and in May 2025, the Delhi HC set it aside, holding that it was contrary to Indian public policy and that specific performance could not be granted for an incomplete commercial arrangement. Zostel later withdrew its challenge before the Supreme Court in July 2025 and filed a fresh appeal before the Delhi HC under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act. The matter remains pending. The dispute resurfaced after OYO confidentially filed its IPO papers in December 2025.
paragraph5: Zostel then sought directions to escrow 7% of OYO’s equity shares and urged SEBI to closely scrutinise the company’s IPO disclosures. PRISM filed its updated DRHP in June this year. The ₹6,650 Cr public issue, comprising entirely a fresh issue of shares, is aimed at repaying or prepaying certain borrowings and supporting the company’s growth initiatives.

title: HoverAir unveils the Versa modular pocket gimbal camera that transforms into a self-flying drone — Modular camera transforms into an auto-tracking drone by magnetically snapping together for instant palm launch and AI tracking
title_bn: HoverAir unveils the Versa modular pocket gimbal camera that transforms into a self-flying drone — Modular camera transforms into an auto-tracking drone by magnetically snapping together for instant palm launch and AI tracking
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Have you ever wanted a pocket gimbal camera and a selfie drone that follows your around autonomously in one device? That's what the HoverAir Versa offers with a transforming, two-in-one body that can make filming yourself from all sorts of angles as
paragraph1: (Image credit: HoverAir on YouTube) HoverAir, makers of self-flying selfie drones, have just unveiled the HoverAir Versa, combining their existing aerial expertise with the convenience of a pocket camera. At its core, the Versa is a high-end stabilized pocket gimbal camera, like the DJI Osmo, but it can magnetically snap onto a drone body and transform into a cinematic selfie drone. It's designed to tackle two different product categories simultaneously, but with the same goal of making it as easy as possible to film yourself (or others). HOVERAir VERSA | This Pocket Camera Can Fly - YouTube Watch On The Versa is actually HoverAir's first-ever pocket camera. It features a three-axis gimbal, which means it can adjust for tilt, yawn, and pitch to make sure your footage turns out stable. Compared to other options on the market, no pocket camera offers more than two-axis stabilization.
paragraph2: It has a rotating screen and the accompanying controls for the camera, along with RGB accent lighting that also works as a status indicator. Overall, it looks like a pretty run-of-the-mill, well-made pocket camera. (Image credit: HoverAir on YouTube)But the magic happens when you bring out the wings. A small, foldable drone body can magnetically attach to the camera unit via pogo pins located at the back of the device. Once connected, you just unfold the wings, gently tap the top, and it takes off right from your palm. There is no external controller needed because the device uses AI to track and follow you automatically.
paragraph3: It has 10+ intelligent modes that can film you from any direction with AI-assisted framing, along with a neat 360° feature as well. (Image credit: HoverAir on YouTube)In this mode, called 3D Worlds, the drone flies around to snap pictures of the scene from different angles and composites them into a single 360° scene that can be explored and shared later. Technically, this would be the third audience the Versa is trying to cater to — the Insta360 crowd, though that's real-time 360° video recording that you can also generously manipulate in post, so not exactly comparable. Still, it's a neat trick, and we'll have to see how well HoverAir implements it.We don't have a price or release date; just a bunch of teasers so far that say it's coming soon. As such, specs are also up in the air, but the company is touting class-leading performance with the best dynamic range in the category.
paragraph4: From the promotional material, we can infer that it has a large lens, and the drone body looks very compact. If HoverAir's previous selfie drones are anything to go by, the Versa could have support for up to 8K video in 10-bit Log or HLG, along with rapid flying speeds of up to 45 km/h. (Image credit: HoverAir on YouTube)The test footage on HoverAir's website and the video we attached above look really impressive. The ingenuity of the concept warrants both excitement and skepticism, but it's undeniable that the Versa kind of feels magical. Nothing like it exists in the market today, and if the company can already ship excellent selfie drones like the X1 series, and pocket cameras aren't exactly rocket science, it stands to reason that harmonizing the two together is the only challenge for the Versa. When he’s not working, you’ll find him bending tubes for his ever-evolving custom water-loop gaming rig or benchmarking the latest CPUs and GPUs just for fun.
