title: 8 free Android productivity apps I can’t live without in 2026
title_bn: 8 free Android productivity apps I can’t live without in 2026
author: TechPulse
excerpt: My current favorite apps for getting things done.
paragraph1: Yash Wate / Android AuthorityI use a bunch of apps on my phone and computer every day. Aside from essential ones, such as Bitwarden and Google Authenticator, these include plenty of productivity apps that help me get things done — both at work and in my personal life.While I pay for a few of these apps, most are either completely free or offer a feature-rich free plan that serves my needs just fine. Here’s a look at my current favorite stack of free productivity apps that actually work and make my life easier — all of which are available on Android.What's that one ultimate productivity app you can't live without?17 votesNotesnookMegan Ellis / Android AuthorityNotesnook is a free, open-source note-taking app that uses end-to-end encryption to protect your notes. I switched to Notesnook from Simplenote a few weeks back and use it for quick note-taking — jotting down information, thoughts, and ideas I frequently need. And it keeps my notes synced across all my devices so I can view or edit them on any device.What I like most about Notesnook is its comprehensive free plan. It has all the features I need in a note-taking app, such as a rich-text editor and support for attachments, tables, and checklists. Plus, there are organizational features such as notebooks, folders and subfolders, tags, and colors to help organize notes more effectively.ObsidianNathan Drescher / Android AuthorityObsidian is another popular free note-taking app I use. It’s my go-to app for storing structured and permanent notes. In other words, I use Obsidian as a personal knowledge base, where I research my personal projects, take notes on new skills I’m learning, track books and blogs to read, and keep tabs on my supplements, among other things.I’ve set up Obsidian to sync notes across all my devices using the free Remotely Save plugin.
paragraph2: Speaking of plugins, that’s where Obsidian’s true power lies; you can find plenty of useful plugins to extend the app’s functionality. Some of my favorite plugins include Bases, Graph View, Slash Commands, Advanced Tables, Excalidraw, QuickAdd, Templater, and Linter.TickTickDhruv Bhutani / Android AuthorityTickTick is one of the best to-do apps for keeping up with everyday tasks. I’ve been using it for several years now, and I have nothing to complain about. While it isn’t a completely free app, its free tier offers all the features I need, such as text formatting, attachments, checklists, subtasks, tags, and comments.One of my favorite TickTick features is Smart Recognition. Thanks to it, I can type, say, “meeting tomorrow at 8 PM” to create a quick task entry and save those extra clicks or taps for selecting the date and time manually.Another handy TickTick feature is recurrent tasks. I use it to remind myself of my recurrent tasks, like bill payments, generating invoices, renewing insurance, and more, every month. I also like the ability to assign priority levels to my tasks, so I know what needs immediate attention and what can take a back seat.TrelloYash Wate / Android AuthorityTrello is a project management app, and I use it to track my tasks for different clients every week, as well as the progress of my personal projects. I prefer it over other apps, such as Asana, since none of my other clients use it, so I don’t have to juggle between two accounts. I also like Trello because it offers a generous free plan, and its Kanban-style workflow feels more intuitive for managing daily tasks.Among other things, I find Trello’s custom fields option really handy. Using it, I can add two dates to my tasks: one for when it’s due date for the publication and the other “do by” for my own.
paragraph3: I also like the subtasks feature. It lets me break down a task for, say, a review into “draft,” “take product shots,” and “edit,” making it easier to track my progress. Finally, there’s the filter feature, which allows me to filter my cards by status and labels to review my work for different clients at the end of each month.Toggl TrackYash Wate / Android AuthorityToggl Track is a time-tracking app that helps me log work hours and the time I spend on each task for all my clients every day. The best part is it’s super easy to use. All I need to do is start the timer before I begin working on a task and stop it when I’m done. Toggle Track then saves the time and lets me add more details about the session, such as a description and project name. I also prefer adding a tag to group similar work sessions.Subsequently, I can go to the calendar tab in the Toggl Track app to see a summary of how I spent the entire month. Toggl Track also has some handy widgets. My favorite is the one that lets you monitor and stop an active session right from the phone. I’ve found this useful at times when I’ve left my desk without stopping the timer on my Mac. Besides, the Toggl Track app has an auto-tracker feature that automatically records the time you spend on your computer, though I prefer to keep it disabled.AirtableYash Wate / Android AuthorityAirtable is my database app of choice for storing data in a structured manner. It essentially offers a board with multiple rows and columns, similar to Excel spreadsheets, where I can enter my data and analyze it using different views as needed.
paragraph4: I started using Airtable to keep tabs on my review units. That way, I know which products I’ve returned and which ones are still with me.Over time, I’ve found some more useful cases for Airtable. I now have a board to track my investments, with comments on the rationale for each and the returns over the last few years. Then there’s one to keep records of my office inventories, so I can refer to it whenever I can’t remember where I kept an item. I’ve also set up a board to save products (watches, tech accessories, etc.) that I want to buy.Raindrop.ioMegan Ellis / Android AuthorityRaindrop.io is an all-in-one bookmark manager app. I switched to it after Pocket shut down and have been using it since to save everything from articles and pages to images and videos from the web that I may need later.Depending on whether I’m on my phone or my computer, I use either the share menu or the browser extension to save items to Raindrop. I then add tags or move items to a relevant folder (or collection) if one exists, so it’s easier to find them later. When I feel lazy or can’t locate an item manually, I use the Raindrop search with search parameters. It’s surprisingly good and returns matching results in seconds.
paragraph5: MacroDroidTushar Mehta / Android AuthorityMacroDroid is one of the best Android automation apps. Thanks to it, I’ve automated a bunch of repetitive tasks on my phone, so I don’t have to perform them manually. All I need to do is create a macro, which involves choosing an appropriate trigger and an action to execute when that trigger gets triggered.For example, I’ve created an automation that automatically deletes screenshots on my phone every 30 days. Similarly, I have one that automatically rotates my phone’s screen when I open and close apps like YouTube and Netflix, so I don’t have to toggle screen orientation manually. I’ve also created a macro that automatically starts my favorite playlist in Spotify when I connect my phone to my car.What's your favorite Android productivity app?15 votesThe above apps greatly simplify various everyday tasks for me across all my devices. All of these apps, except for MacroDroid, are available on all major mobile and desktop platforms — and every single one is available on Android.FollowThank you for being part of our community. Read our Comment Policy before posting.

In other words, I use Obsidian as a personal knowledge base, where I research my personal projects, take notes on new skills I’m learning, track books and blogs to read, and keep tabs on my supplements, among other things.I’ve set up Obsidian to sync notes across all my devices using the free Remotely Save plugin.
bangla_paragraph2: Speaking of plugins, that’s where Obsidian’s true power lies; you can find plenty of useful plugins to extend the app’s functionality. Some of my favorite plugins include Bases, Graph View, Slash Commands, Advanced Tables, Excalidraw, QuickAdd, Templater, and Linter.TickTickDhruv Bhutani / Android AuthorityTickTick is one of the best to-do apps for keeping up with everyday tasks. I’ve been using it for several years now, and I have nothing to complain about. While it isn’t a completely free app, its free tier offers all the features I need, such as text formatting, attachments, checklists, subtasks, tags, and comments.One of my favorite TickTick features is Smart Recognition. Thanks to it, I can type, say, “meeting tomorrow at 8 PM” to create a quick task entry and save those extra clicks or taps for selecting the date and time manually.Another handy TickTick feature is recurrent tasks. I use it to remind myself of my recurrent tasks, like bill payments, generating invoices, renewing insurance, and more, every month. I also like the ability to assign priority levels to my tasks, so I know what needs immediate attention and what can take a back seat.TrelloYash Wate / Android AuthorityTrello is a project management app, and I use it to track my tasks for different clients every week, as well as the progress of my personal projects. I prefer it over other apps, such as Asana, since none of my other clients use it, so I don’t have to juggle between two accounts. I also like Trello because it offers a generous free plan, and its Kanban-style workflow feels more intuitive for managing daily tasks.Among other things, I find Trello’s custom fields option really handy. Using it, I can add two dates to my tasks: one for when it’s due date for the publication and the other “do by” for my own.
bangla_paragraph3: I also like the subtasks feature. It lets me break down a task for, say, a review into “draft,” “take product shots,” and “edit,” making it easier to track my progress. Finally, there’s the filter feature, which allows me to filter my cards by status and labels to review my work for different clients at the end of each month.Toggl TrackYash Wate / Android AuthorityToggl Track is a time-tracking app that helps me log work hours and the time I spend on each task for all my clients every day. The best part is it’s super easy to use. All I need to do is start the timer before I begin working on a task and stop it when I’m done. Toggle Track then saves the time and lets me add more details about the session, such as a description and project name. I also prefer adding a tag to group similar work sessions.Subsequently, I can go to the calendar tab in the Toggl Track app to see a summary of how I spent the entire month. Toggl Track also has some handy widgets. My favorite is the one that lets you monitor and stop an active session right from the phone. I’ve found this useful at times when I’ve left my desk without stopping the timer on my Mac. Besides, the Toggl Track app has an auto-tracker feature that automatically records the time you spend on your computer, though I prefer to keep it disabled.AirtableYash Wate / Android AuthorityAirtable is my database app of choice for storing data in a structured manner. It essentially offers a board with multiple rows and columns, similar to Excel spreadsheets, where I can enter my data and analyze it using different views as needed.
bangla_paragraph4: I started using Airtable to keep tabs on my review units. That way, I know which products I’ve returned and which ones are still with me.Over time, I’ve found some more useful cases for Airtable. I now have a board to track my investments, with comments on the rationale for each and the returns over the last few years. Then there’s one to keep records of my office inventories, so I can refer to it whenever I can’t remember where I kept an item. I’ve also set up a board to save products (watches, tech accessories, etc.) that I want to buy.Raindrop.ioMegan Ellis / Android AuthorityRaindrop.io is an all-in-one bookmark manager app. I switched to it after Pocket shut down and have been using it since to save everything from articles and pages to images and videos from the web that I may need later.Depending on whether I’m on my phone or my computer, I use either the share menu or the browser extension to save items to Raindrop. I then add tags or move items to a relevant folder (or collection) if one exists, so it’s easier to find them later. When I feel lazy or can’t locate an item manually, I use the Raindrop search with search parameters. It’s surprisingly good and returns matching results in seconds.
bangla_paragraph5: MacroDroidTushar Mehta / Android AuthorityMacroDroid is one of the best Android automation apps. Thanks to it, I’ve automated a bunch of repetitive tasks on my phone, so I don’t have to perform them manually. All I need to do is create a macro, which involves choosing an appropriate trigger and an action to execute when that trigger gets triggered.For example, I’ve created an automation that automatically deletes screenshots on my phone every 30 days. Similarly, I have one that automatically rotates my phone’s screen when I open and close apps like YouTube and Netflix, so I don’t have to toggle screen orientation manually. I’ve also created a macro that automatically starts my favorite playlist in Spotify when I connect my phone to my car.What's your favorite Android productivity app?15 votesThe above apps greatly simplify various everyday tasks for me across all my devices. All of these apps, except for MacroDroid, are available on all major mobile and desktop platforms — and every single one is available on Android.FollowThank you for being part of our community. title: NASA modded space station's laptops so everyone could use the same charger — standardizing ISS chargers eliminated useless weight and reduced failure points
title_bn: NASA modded space station's laptops so everyone could use the same charger — standardizing ISS chargers eliminated useless weight and reduced failure points
author: TechPulse
excerpt: NASA ensured that all laptops destined for use in the International Space Station had the same 'cannon' power connector by implementing a modification.
paragraph1: NASA ensured that all laptops destined for use in the International Space Station (ISS) had the same power connector. Engineer George Roush, who has a certain fondness for space tech, recalled details of this laptop modification earlier this week. Standardizing on a single ‘cannon plug’ meant that instead of requiring a multitude of different chargers, ISS visitors could plug into the onboard DC power outlets in a standard fashion. Roush took the photos shared below during a visit to the NASA Stennis visitor center.Since you all care (thank you for that, by the way) here's the answer: That's not an ethernet port at all! It's a modem port! Modem ports are useless on the ISS.
paragraph2: So, NASA replaced this useless port with a new power port. Taking 9 different laptop chargers into space sounds… pic.twitter.com/ZLcqcEOHVfAugust 2, 2026Laptops destined to be used on the ISS would have their modem ports removed and replaced by the cannon plug you can see in the engineer’s photos. Of course, modem ports would be useless on the ISS, so that’s why they would be replaced with this modification. In space, every gram, every connector, and every failure mode matters, which makes this power standardization a smart move.Sources indicate that Lockheed Martin was contracted to make these modifications to the ThinkPads and other machines that ended up being taken to space.
paragraph3: Roush also discusses networking/comms on the ISS, which relied on the MIL-STD-1553 system, rather than Ethernet.Laptops with built-in telephony modem ports certainly date this story. However, we must remember that the ISS was constructed in the late 1990s when modems were still essential for PCs. The first crews docked in 2000.Original web sources are vanishingWhen refreshing his knowledge about this laptops-in-space mod, the space enthusiast and engineer was struck by another realization, which he found troubling. The NASA Stennis visitor center had barely any information about the laptops or the cannon plug modification that was on display.Turning to some online resources he remembers referring to previously, Roush noticed a lot of them had disappeared.
paragraph4: “The old internet is dying, and with it, we risk losing a lot of useful history,” said the engineer. “I fear that the false belief of the 'eternal' internet will cause otherwise recorded history to be lost when the servers shut down.”Though some resources may still be able to be unearthed via the Wayback Machine, it seems perilous that so much web history is archived by a charity (The Internet Archive). In May, we reported that the internet is getting harder to archive because the AI boom has caused a storage crisis, with both NAND and mechanical drives facing shortages. This means skyrocketing storage bills to support the activities of the Wayback Machine.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.HP replaced all the ISS laptops in April 2026The astronauts in the ISS aren’t still using old modded laptops like the one showcased in the NASA Stennis visitor center.
paragraph5: The latest updates came in April this year, with over 100 HP Z Workstations packing a mix of Core Ultra 9 processors and RTX Pro Blackwell graphics sent into orbit.HP talks about putting these PCs through two years of rigorous testing ahead of deployment. We don’t get much in the way of technical info from its release, but again, it was recognized that a single power standard was important. The computer maker supplies universal AC/DC power adapters with its latest crop of space laptops that are specially designed to function on both the ISS and Earth. He enjoys covering the full breadth of PC tech; from business and semiconductor design to products approaching the edge of reason.

title: Claude Code Adds Cross-Session Messaging on macOS
title_bn: Claude Code Adds Cross-Session Messaging on macOS
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Anthropic has updated Claude Code so that separate coding sessions can message each other directly, removing the need to manually copy context between Terminal windows. The company shipped the feature in Claude Code version 2.1.224, released on Frida
paragraph1: Anthropic has updated Claude Code so that separate coding sessions can message each other directly, removing the need to manually copy context between Terminal windows. The company shipped the feature in Claude Code version 2.1.224, released on Friday for macOS and Linux. Two new tools power it: ListAgents, which finds other active sessions running on the Mac, and SendMessage, which delivers the message. A session that receives one shows it as a labeled card with a link back to the sender. According to Anthropic's documentation, only text passes between sessions, not conversation history, files, or permissions.
paragraph2: One session can warn another when a change breaks something it depends on, or pass along an answer another session is waiting on, and Anthropic says an incoming message can't approve a permission request or change a session's settings on its own. New in Claude Code: your sessions can now message each other. Instead of having to re-explain yourself in another session, you can now tell Claude to do it. It sends a summary (not your history or files), and the other session picks it up mid-task. pic.twitter.com/PtNsfXeQXP — ClaudeDevs (@ClaudeDevs) August 7, 2026 The feature sits alongside Claude Code's existing subagents and Agent Teams tools, but connects sessions a user is already running separately on their Mac rather than ones Claude spawns and manages itself.
paragraph3: Messages between sessions on the same Mac stay local and never reach Anthropic's servers. Between different machines, messaging works only as a reply through Remote Control, the feature that connects a Mac terminal to the Claude apps for iOS and Android. Cross session messaging requires macOS or Linux with Claude Code 2.1.224 or later and isn't available on Windows. It was released alongside 31 other changes in the same release, including a new claude self-hosted-runner command for Team and Enterprise plans. title: iPhone 17 Prices Could Rise as Soon as Monday, Rumor Claims
title_bn: iPhone 17 Prices Could Rise as Soon as Monday, Rumor Claims
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Apple could raise iPhone 17 prices as soon as Monday, August 10, according to a new rumor, well before the wider round of increases expected with next month's iPhone 18 Pro launch. Weibo leaker "Fixed Focus Digital" said in a post yesterday that rumo
paragraph1: Apple could raise iPhone 17 prices as soon as Monday, August 10, according to a new rumor, well before the wider round of increases expected with next month's iPhone 18 Pro launch. Weibo leaker "Fixed Focus Digital" said in a post yesterday that rumors are circulating about an ‌iPhone 17‌ price change taking effect on August 10. The leaker was noncommittal about whether prices will actually move, though the post claimed with more certainty that Apple has called off plans to raise production capacity on some lines from 15% to 30%. It's not clear from the post which components or products that capacity change refers to.
paragraph2: Apple raised prices on Macs, iPads, and most other devices in June, citing soaring memory and storage costs, but left the iPhone, Apple Watch, AirPods, Studio Display, and accessories untouched. Apple's next round of pricing changes is widely rumored to center on the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌. Apple is expected to launch the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌, ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, and its first foldable iPhone next month, with the standard iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e not arriving until spring 2027. The ‌iPhone 17‌ is set to remain Apple's mainstream option well into next year, which could give Apple sufficient reason to adjust its pricing independently of the new lineup.
paragraph3: If Apple does raise ‌iPhone 17‌ prices this Monday, it remains to be seen whether the increase would apply across the whole lineup, including the iPhone 17e ($599), ‌iPhone 17‌ ($799), iPhone Air ($999), iPhone 17 Pro ($1,099), and ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌ Max ($1,199), or whether only select models will be affected. title: Don’t wait for the Pixel 11: Why you should buy the Pixel 10 right now
title_bn: Don’t wait for the Pixel 11: Why you should buy the Pixel 10 right now
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Be smart and save you money with the Pixel 10. You won't be missing much.
paragraph1: The Google Pixel 11 series is nearly here, and a massive leak just a few days ago pretty much revealed all the important bits we’ve been dying to know. While nothing is official until Google takes the stage on August 12, it seems to align with most of the rumors we’ve been seeing this year.The Pixel 11 Pro series will once again shine the brightest, quite literally this time, with the new HiLight notification light. But there doesn’t seem to be much in store for the base Pixel 11, which begs the question — should you simply grab the Pixel 10 at a discount today?I think you should. Here’s why.Would you buy a higher priced Google Pixel 11?1342 votesThe Pixel 11 is more expensive, but it doesn’t have much to show for it The Pixel 11 is expected to start at $899 in the US, $100 more than the Pixel 10’s $799 starting price. To be fair, the $899 is for 256GB of storage, not 128GB, which puts both models on equal footing when you match their storage tiers. For the first time, you’ll also have a choice of 512GB storage for the base Pixel, which is nice.The Pixel 10 was already quite a big upgrade to the Pixel 9, so I wasn’t expecting anything crazy with the Pixel 11. And, it doesn’t seem like we’re getting much either. There’ll be the new Tensor G6 processor with a heavy focus on on-device AI processing, and I’m curious to see what progress Google has made in power efficiency and performance compared to Qualcomm’s offering.For the first time, you’ll also have a choice of 512GB storage for the base Pixel.
paragraph2: We’ll be getting new colors for sure, and purple or lilac seems to be one of the hero colors for the Pixel 11, based on recent leaked marketing images. Here, we see the camera bar is thinner, and it has the same all-glass design as the Pro models.The Pixel 11 is also expected to deliver “more than 30 hours” of battery life, while charging is 25% faster than the Pixel 10, according to leaked images. These hourly runtimes usually should be taken with a grain of salt, though, as they are achieved under controlled testing conditions. Still, this should come as some relief to the respondents of our poll, where a majority want improved battery life in the Pixel 11 series.One camera improvement we know is coming to the Pixel 11 is zoom, which now goes up to 30x from 20x. Apart from these things, though, the leaks don’t point to any other major changes. The rest of the cameras, display specs, and dimensions seem similar to, or the same as, the Pixel 10.The Pixel 10 is still a great buy in 2026Rita El Khoury / Android AuthorityPixel 10The Pixel 10 is still a fantastic phone a year later, and will receive six more years of OS and security updates. It was also the first base-model Pixel with a telephoto camera, something I’ve been wanting for years (take a hint, Apple). Although the Pixel 10 camera’s image quality doesn’t always match up to the Pro models, it’s good enough for most scenarios. Google really narrowed the feature gap between the base and Pro Pixels with the Pixel 10, so you’re not really missing much.The design and build quality of the Pixel 10 are great. It’s quite compact and fairly light, which makes it easy to carry around.
paragraph3: Battery life is decent, too, depending on how you use it. The big battery feature in my book is the built-in magnets for Qi2 charging, something that very few Android phones have even today. The Pixel 10 works beautifully with any MagSafe accessory, without needing a special case.Google really minimized the feature gap between the base and Pro Pixels with the Pixel 10.The Pixel 10 is IP68 rated for dust and water resistance. It has a bright and vivid 6.3-inch display with a peak brightness of up to 3,000 nits. Touch response and sunlight legibility have been fantastic so far, so no complaints here.In terms of performance, the Tensor G5 in the Pixel 10 once again prioritizes AI efficiency over raw performance. Having said that, we’ve noticed that gaming performance has improved with Android 17, even though a few kinks still remain. Sadly, the Tensor G6 in the Pixel 11 is expected to do more of the same, so if you’re expecting Snapdragon Elite-level performance, you’re probably going to be disappointed.Add it all up, and the Pixel 10 makes a compelling case for itself over the Pixel 11. For anyone who’s still on a Pixel 7/7a or older, upgrading to the Pixel 10 should feel like a big generational leap.Grab a good deal on the Pixel 10 todayRobert Triggs / Android AuthorityGoogle hasn’t officially slashed the price of the Pixel 10 yet, but that’s certainly coming once the Pixel 11 is out.
paragraph4: In the meantime, you can find good savings from other retailers and e-tailers.Walmart is selling the 128GB Pixel 10 for just $710 right now, though this price is for the Lemon Grass colorway only. The other colors are retailing at $750, which is still lower than Google’s official price. The Pixel 10 is often discounted on Amazon, so keep an eye out for deals there.If you’re not happy buying unlocked, your carrier will most certainly have deals running on the Pixel 10. Whether it’s through a trade-in or opting for it on contract outright, you should be able to get the Pixel 10 for a lower monthly installment today. Back in May, T-Mobile was giving away a free Pixel 10 as a loyalty perk to its high-value customers, with some caveats, of course.MVNOs are also a good place to look for deals. Boost Mobile, for instance, has the Pixel 10 128GB for $300, with no trade-in required. The catch here is that you have to take the $60/ month Unlimited Premium plan. Mint Mobile also offers something similar for the Pixel 10, but it’s currently out of stock. title: Centre Seeks Technical Changes From Meta To Tackle Deepfakes, Child Abuse Material
title_bn: Centre Seeks Technical Changes From Meta To Tackle Deepfakes, Child Abuse Material
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The Centre’s discussions with Meta have moved into a technical phase after two days of intensive questioning over deepfakes, child…
paragraph1: SUMMARYThe Centre has moved discussions with Meta to the technical stage and asked the company to take specific measures on deepfakes, CSAM, and unlabelled AI-generated content The talks indicate tighter government scrutiny of Meta's content moderation practices and compliance with Indian laws, with officials expected to closely monitor corrective measures Meta outlined its proposed solutions during technical discussions, with another round of talks likely next week The Centre’s discussions with Meta have moved into a technical phase after two days of intensive questioning over deepfakes, child sexual abuse material (CSAM), unlabelled AI-generated content, and the company’s content recommendation algorithms. During the third day of discussions with MeitY officials yesterday, Meta’s global team, led by global affairs chief Joel Kaplan, explained how its systems work and outlined measures it plans to deploy to address the Centre’s concerns. A PTI report, citing sources, said the government has asked Meta to implement specific measures and report back on the outcomes. Officials are expected to regularly review the company’s progress, with another meeting likely to be held next week.
paragraph2: One of the key concerns raised by the government was the reappearance and continued circulation of harmful AI-generated content even after it had been flagged. Officials also questioned why unlabelled AI-generated videos remain visible on Meta’s platforms despite the government’s push for synthetic content to be appropriately identified and labelled. The Centre has also asked Meta to strengthen human oversight in content moderation, with greater emphasis on Indian languages as well as local cultural and social contexts. Meta told officials it has solutions to address deepfakes, CSAM, bot accounts and synthetic content, and explained how these measures could be deployed across its platforms.
paragraph3: The PTI report said government sources described the discussions as an effort to ensure Meta complies with Indian laws rather than an attempt at censorship. Officials are expected to continue engaging with the company as it implements corrective measures. Meta Under Pressure The technical discussions followed two days of meetings in which IT minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and IT secretary S Krishnan questioned Meta’s global team over its compliance with Indian laws, content recommendation algorithms, and platform safeguards. The government had summoned Meta after Facebook temporarily restricted a video posted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
paragraph4: The video remained unavailable for nearly five to six hours before being restored, with Meta attributing the incident to an error in its AI-powered content filters. Later, Meta apologised, while government sources said the apology came from CEO Mark Zuckerberg. The issue also came under the scrutiny of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Communications and Information Technology, which sought an “unqualified apology” from Zuckerberg and warned that Meta’s safe harbour protection under Section 79 of the IT Act could be reconsidered. The panel also raised concerns over CSAM and content targeting women, directing digital platforms to take immediate action.
paragraph5: Meanwhile, the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) is investigating allegations that CSAM-linked advertisements appeared on Meta’s platforms, while the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has directed the Delhi Police to probe similar allegations involving paid Instagram advertisements. The government has also questioned Meta over the paid promotion of potentially harmful content, recommendation algorithms, and safeguards for prominent accounts. The Centre is expected to continue discussions with Meta next week as it reviews the company’s progress on the measures discussed.

title: Nitecore’s latest power bank is the lightest and most compact yet
title_bn: Nitecore’s latest power bank is the lightest and most compact yet
author: TechPulse
excerpt: There's two things you should know about me, your intrepid reviewer: I hate the feature creep associated with modern power banks, and I love shaving grams off the gear I carry when backpacking, bikepacking, and trail running. So imagine my delight wh
paragraph1: There’s two things you should know about me, your intrepid reviewer: I hate the feature creep associated with modern power banks, and I love shaving grams off the gear I carry when backpacking, bikepacking, and trail running. So imagine my delight when Nitecore released a new generation of its ultralight NB10000 battery. After a few weeks with it I can confidently say: Haribo be damned!The $83.95 NB10000 Gen 4 weighs just 146 grams, according to my scale, and measures 1.45 x 11.6 x 4.68cm (0.57 x 4.57 x 1.84 inches), according to Nitecore’s spec sheet. That makes it the lightest and most compact 10,000mAh power bank I can find.
paragraph2: Even when factoring in the extra 6 grams added by the included USB-C lanyard, it still beats the previous ultralight champ: Nitecore’s NB10000 Gen 3. The secret to the Gen 4’s impressive weight is a silicon-carbon anode, the same battery tech increasingly appearing in flagship smartphones, including Samsung’s.As small as it is, the Gen 4’s 39Wh battery still fully recharged my aging iPhone 15 Pro twice, with a few watt-hours left in the tank. And with up to 22.5W of output, it can even top-up my 14-inch MacBook Pro when needed. It also supports pass-through to charge your gadgets as the power bank itself charges.Have I found power bank perfection? Almost.8Verge Score$84The GoodClass-leading energy densitySmallest and lightest 10,000mAh aroundGreat for endurance athletes and backpackersImpressive water resistanceThe BadExpensiveKnock-to-wake is hit-or-missSilly RGB lightingI like that the NB10000 Gen 4 gets all the basics right. It has a simple, four-element indicator to show the battery level, which I much prefer over a fancy display. It’s constructed out of carbon fiber sheets and offers IPX7 protection against water ingress, allowing it to withstand rain or even temporary submersion – exactly what you want from an adventure battery.In my testing, I measured 33.
paragraph3: 58Wh of the claimed 39Wh capacity for an 86.1 percent efficiency. That’s a pretty good result for a premium power bank and a slight improvement on the 33.33Wh we measured on the Gen 3 model. That works out to 229.98Wh/kg of delivered energy, or 220.90Wh/kg with the cable — class-leading results, either way. The NB10000 Gen 4 supports PD, QC3.0, and Huawei’s SCP charging protocols.The Gen 4 battery on top of an iPhone 15 Pro. It’s very small for the charge capacity it holds.The RGB lights are pretty but a little superfluous and that button is touch-sensitive instead of mechanical.
paragraph4: Silly.Carbon fiber shell with strong IPX7 resistance to water ingress.Supports pass-through charging to charge and be charged simultaneously.The Gen 4 model also didn’t suffer from the overheating and shutdown issues we saw when the Gen 3 would run low on juice. I did, however, see a temporary interruption in power delivery when the Gen 4 unit was almost fully depleted, but that’s only because I had a meter attached — otherwise I wouldn’t have known since it continued charging almost immediately.The only thing that could be considered superfluous is the animated RGB lighting that flows around the dual USB-C ports. The lights are there to guide you to the USB-C ports in a dark tent, says Nitecore, but you can also… feel them. Give the battery a double-knock near the top and the lights (and battery indicator) illuminate. This can be helpful if wearing gloves since Nitecore inexplicably opted for a touch-sensitive wake button on the Gen 4. Fortunately, that so-called “Touch Button” did reliably sense my wet finger in testing. The knock-to-wake feature seemed to only work about 75 percent of the time, but it, and the RGB lights, can be disabled if you want.1/8The lanyard is actually a braided USB-C cable rated for up to 60W.
paragraph5: The lights will also glow yellow (regular mode) or green (eco) after a long press of the power button if you want to toggle between full power and extended life, respectively. Eco mode works by dropping the output to a slow 5W (5V at 1A) max. This can keep the power bank from automatically shutting off when charging low-draw devices like headlamps, watches, or wireless earbuds. It can also yield a little more total charge capacity by producing less heat waste, and allow the battery to operate closer to its native voltage resulting in less conversion loss.The Nitecore NB10000 Gen 4 is the ideal power bank for endurance athletes, backpackers, or anyone looking for an ultralight and ultracompact power bank that mostly avoids feature creep. The only real negative is the price, having gone up to $83.95 since the launch of the $64.95 Gen 3 model two years ago. That makes the Gen 4 power bank two to three times more expensive than the typical 10,000mAh power bank, but it can save you 50 grams or more. That’s a price premium I can see lots of active, outdoorsy people happily paying for.All photos by Thomas Ricker / The VergeFollow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.

title: Swiggy, Zomato, Zepto May Face EV Mandate, 2% Welfare Levy In Maharashtra
title_bn: Swiggy, Zomato, Zepto May Face EV Mandate, 2% Welfare Levy In Maharashtra
author: TechPulse
excerpt: New-age tech consumer tech companies like Swiggy, Zomato, Zepto, and Meesho could face higher costs in Maharashtra as the state…
paragraph1: SUMMARYMaharashtra plans to bring food delivery, quick commerce and ecommerce platforms under its proposed bike-taxi rules, introducing an EV mandate and a 2% rider welfare levy The move could increase compliance costs for platforms and expand state-level regulation of gig workers The proposal also includes GPS tracking, insurance cover and a welfare fund, but it remains unclear how the 2% levy will be calculated for delivery platforms New-age tech consumer tech companies like Swiggy, Zomato, Zepto, and Meesho could face higher costs in Maharashtra as the state plans to bring food delivery and ecommerce platforms under its bike-taxi rules. According to a report by The Indian Express, the proposed amendments to the Maharashtra Bike-Taxi Rules, 2025, would require covered platforms to deploy EVs, enable GPS-based tracking of drivers and vehicles, provide insurance cover, and contribute 2% of each trip’s fare to a driver welfare fund. The proposed welfare fund would finance benefits such as pensions, accident insurance, EV purchase loans, and education assistance for drivers’ children. However, unlike bike-taxi services, food delivery, quick commerce and ecommerce platforms do not operate on fixed ride fares, making it unclear whether the proposed levy would be calculated on the amount paid to delivery partners for each order or based on the distance travelled. If approved, the amendments would bring delivery service providers, ecommerce and quick commerce platforms under Maharashtra’s bike-taxi regulatory framework for the first time.
paragraph2: At present, Maharashtra does not have a dedicated state-level regulatory framework governing food delivery and ecommerce platforms. These businesses are primarily regulated under central laws, including the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, and the Code on Social Security, 2020. The proposal is currently under review by Maharashtra’s law and judiciary department and is yet to receive final approval. Transport minister Pratap Sarnaik told the publication that the proposed framework would apply to bikes undertaking trips of less than 15 km, with the EV and other compliance requirements coming into effect once the amendments are cleared. The state also plans to launch a dedicated portal, developed by the state transport commissioner, to track vehicles operating under the bike-taxi framework in real time.
paragraph3: States Tighten Gig Platform Rules The Maharashtra proposal comes amid growing state-level efforts to regulate gig work and strengthen social security for platform workers. In Karnataka, industry bodies and platforms including IAMAI, Eternal, Swiggy, Zepto, Urban Company, Uber, and Meesho’s logistics arm Valmo Transportation have challenged the constitutional validity of the Karnataka Platform-Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025. The law establishes a welfare board and fund for gig workers and mandates a welfare contribution from platforms. Earlier this year, Karnataka fixed the levy at 1% per transaction, subject to category-wise caps. Food and grocery delivery platforms face a cap of ₹0.
paragraph4: 50 per transaction, while ride-hailing platforms face caps ranging from ₹0.50 to ₹1, depending on the vehicle category. Platform companies have argued that the legislation creates an additional social security framework despite the Centre’s Code on Social Security, 2020, and warned that varying state-level welfare levies and compliance requirements could significantly increase operating costs for businesses operating across multiple states. The Karnataka High Court has declined to stay the law but granted interim protection from coercive action to the petitioners, subject to them depositing the welfare contribution due for the April-June quarter with the court. The matter is next scheduled for hearing on August 14.
paragraph5: If approved, the Maharashtra proposal would add another layer to the evolving state-level regulatory landscape for gig workers and platform businesses, potentially increasing compliance costs for food delivery, quick commerce and ecommerce companies operating across multiple states.

title: OpenAI says it slowed Astra model development over security concerns
title_bn: OpenAI says it slowed Astra model development over security concerns
author: TechPulse
excerpt: OpenAI said this model, which is still in development, reached its "critical cybersecurity threshold," meaning it could independently identify and carry out cyberattacks against traditionally well-protected real-world systems.
paragraph1: Image Credits:SeongJoon Cho/Bloomberg / Getty Images 3:48 PM PDT · August 7, 2026 OpenAI said Friday it has suspended work on some aspects of its upcoming model Astra after an internal review found it had made significant advancements in agentic coding and cybersecurity — enough to warrant concern over its capabilities. OpenAI said in a blog post Friday that this model, which is still in development, reached its “critical cybersecurity threshold,” meaning it could independently identify and carry out cyberattacks against traditionally well-protected real-world systems. Under the company’s “Preparedness Framework,” which it created in 2023, this triggered additional safeguards. “While we continue to benchmark and assess this model, our preliminary evaluations indicate strong enough performance that we cannot rule out Critical capability level at this time,” OpenAI wrote. “Astra is an upcoming model, and was not involved in exploiting Hugging Face.” The disclosure highlights an unusual moment in the topsy-turvy and still nascent frontier AI labs sector.
paragraph2: Companies across every industry hold back products over potential risks, including for safety and cybersecurity concerns. But they rarely announce those decisions publicly when it’s a product that is still under development. In this case, OpenAI is already under scrutiny after a different unreleased model breached Hugging Face’s systems during internal testing — the first verifiable incident of an AI lab losing control of its model. Since then, OpenAI and AI labs such as Anthropic have disclosed other incidents in which AI models breached their sandboxes and posed threats during cybersecurity tests. The string of cases — seems like a new disclosure every day now — has triggered varying reactions from cybersecurity experts, lawmakers, and the AI labs themselves. Some express fear and call for stricter oversight.
paragraph3: But there’s also a bit of flexing. In certain circles, any AI lab with a model that has that kind of capability will be seen as an impressive advancement. OpenAI said it was sharing this information because it believes “it’s important to be transparent with the public and the safety and security communities about this potential shift in capabilities.” The AI lab said it’s also taking action, including enacting stricter security controls and pausing internal activities involving Astra that don’t meet these beefed guardrails. OpenAI said it is working with relevant government agencies and “select AI safety organizations” to test the capabilities for this model. title: The gaming site sponsored by Walmart lays off its editorial staff
title_bn: The gaming site sponsored by Walmart lays off its editorial staff
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Restart, a games media website launched in late 2024 that was sponsored by Walmart, has laid off its "entire editorial team," according to a Friday post from Brandy Berthelson, the site's former editor-in-chief. Other staffers have also posted about
paragraph1: Restart’s former editor-in-chief says the ‘entire editorial team’ has been cut.Restart’s former editor-in-chief says the ‘entire editorial team’ has been cut.by Jay PetersAug 7, 2026, 10:05 PM UTCImage: The VergeJay Peters is a senior reporter covering technology, gaming, and more. He joined The Verge in 2019 after nearly two years at Techmeme.
paragraph2: Restart, a games media website launched in late 2024 that was sponsored by Walmart, has laid off its “entire editorial team,” according to a Friday post from Brandy Berthelson, the site’s former editor-in-chief. Other staffers have also posted about being laid off.Restart is operated by Moonrock, a content marketing agency, though its editorial mission page says it’s “powered” by Walmart. That page outlines how Walmart is (or was) involved:When we mention a game, we’ll provide purchase links that will take you to Walmart using a partner tracking code.
paragraph3: This link provides us with 0% of the sale if you decide to buy the product, but it does help Walmart see exactly how customers arrived at the product.According to that page, Restart operated as an “independent site” and said that Walmart “doesn’t influence our editorial direction.”According to that page, Restart operated as an “independent site” and said that Walmart “doesn’t influence our editorial direction.”Basically, Restart was Walmart’s take on something like Game Informer, which used to be owned by GameStop.
paragraph4: A few months before the launch of Restart, GameStop shut Game Informer down, though it’s since been revived under new ownership.Berthelson says she is “not able” to discuss details of the layoffs. One laid off staffer tells The Verge that they signed a severance agreement with Moonrock.As of this writing, Restart remains online.
paragraph5: It’s unclear if Walmart and Moonrock will continue operating the site following the layoffs, and if so, what that will look like. Walmart and Moonrock didn’t immediately reply to requests for comment.Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.Jay PetersThe Verge DailyA free daily digest of the news that matters most.

title: After Rippling blew millions on AI in months, it built an employee ROI tool
title_bn: After Rippling blew millions on AI in months, it built an employee ROI tool
author: TechPulse
excerpt: After its own AI usage wake-up call, Rippling this week unveiled AI Spend Console, a product that tracks individual and team employee AI spending.
paragraph1: HR software provider Rippling this week unveiled AI Spend Console, an anti-tokenmaxxing product that helps a company track and contain its AI spending. One of the most interesting features is that it maps how much individual employees, teams, and roles are spending and if they are genuinely more productive, or generally producing more AI slop. The company promises the tool will show “which engineers have high AI spend whose peers frequently ask them to redo work in code reviews,” the company says in its blog post. The tool was born after Rippling went all in on tokenmaxxing at the start of the year — as so many did — only to discover employees were wildly burning cash. Chief Product Officer Matt MacInnis still recalls the executive team meeting in March when CFO Adam Swiecicki presented a number that shocked them. Rippling was on track to burn 40% of its R&D headcount budget on AI tokens, meaning it was spending as much on tokens as 40% of all the compensation it paid employees in that unit. Millions of dollars. (The R&D org is home to engineering at most tech companies.) Spending was growing by 80% month-over-month, and if that trend continued, the next year it would spend almost as much on AI tokens — 90% — as it spent on its high-paid R&D unit employees. “We were incredulous,” MacInnis told TechCrunch. Management immediately undertook an “urgent” project to understand the spending and what they were getting for that money, he said.
paragraph2: In fact, the launch ad for this new product features Swiecicki sitting on a stool while employees are picking up wads of cash and dumping them into a paper shredder. When Rippling conducted an analysis, it discovered facts like “roughly 10–15% of our employees were driving about 60% of total AI spend. One engineer was spending $50,000 a month,” its blog post shared. Rippling didn’t want to stop AI usage, just rein it in — a lot. It started by negotiating a max spending cap with each of the tools its company used: Cursor, OpenAI, and Anthropic. It immediately found an obvious issue: Employees defaulted to using the most recent, and most expensive, frontier models for all tasks. “The truth is that the inference providers, like Anthropic and OpenAI, have absolutely no incentives to help you control your spend. They have every incentive for it to be a runaway expense, and that’s exactly what they do. They don’t provide you with great usage insight, and they don’t collaborate with one another,” MacInnis said. That was a common early-2026 problem. Now, eight months into the year, enterprises have figured out a couple of things.
paragraph3: First, they know they need multiple models from multiple AI labs at various price points, including a frontier open weight option, perhaps of Chinese origin. Rippling founder and CEO Parker Conrad noted last month that when his company conducted its own benchmarks for its own internal uses, it discovered SpaceX’s Grok was the all-around leader but that “GLM 5.2 is 85% cheaper but [had] nearly identical performance” to the frontier models. (SpaceX now owns Cursor, which offers access to Grok and dozens of other models.) Z.ai’s GLM 5.2 has become a particular favorite Chinese model for coding tasks among tech companies these days. Databricks has also been championing it. Second, enterprises now know they need an AI gateway that routes prompts to the best, most cost-effective model for the task. Rippling came to that conclusion too. So it built its own AI gateway that is also part of this product.
paragraph4: MacInnis says it is possible for enterprises that already use another gateway to still use the AI Spend Console product, though if they want the features that govern spending, they would need to use Rippling’s gateway. AI Spend Console produces dashboards (once known as leaderboards in the tokenmaxxing days) that score attributes such as prompts per day combined with work output (lines of code/pull requests) and spend. With this tool in place, Rippling said it dropped its token spend from 40% of its headcount budget to about 15%. But it didn’t curtail AI usage. The company spent a peak of 605 billion tokens the month the CFO issued his warning, MacInnis shared. In July, internal usage hit 600 billion tokens again, yet “the cost of July’s token spend was 37% of the cost of April’s token spend,” he said. “That’s just because now we’re routing to the more effective models,” he said, joking that “we’re not letting the sales team do grammar updates using Fable.” But technology solutions aren’t enough, Rippling notes. The company found people using AI effectively and made them “AI captains” tasked with assisting the rest of the company. Still, such efforts to use AI beyond engineering are a work in progress, MacInnis says, as software engineers have been the primary users so far. But Rippling is, for example, working on it for customer onboarding teams to automate some mailing data and data-reconciliation tasks.
paragraph5: The dashboard will then measure productivity in terms of onboarding more customers. “We have to be able to link token consumption in G&A functions and in customer-facing functions back to productivity. If we can’t do that, all bets are off on any of this stuff being available to the broader employee base,” MacInnis says. So, if Rippling is an example, tokenmaxxing may have swung so far the other direction that employee AI access may no longer be like Slack or email. If the company can’t measure productivity, then all employees might not have access. As for the product, AI Spend Console is included for Rippling’s HR subscribers, though there are additional AI usage-based costs. It can also be purchased as a stand-alone product and integrated with another HR system of record, MacInnis says. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission. Prior OpenAI models, including GPT–5.6 Sol, were labeled as "High." Astra triggers stricter guidelines in OpenAI's "Preparedness Framework." The guidelines call for caution when developing frontier AI capabilities that create risks of severe harm, and the cybersecurity portion of the framework says OpenAI will implement extra safeguards for models that "create new risks of scaled cyberattacks and vulnerability exploitation." The "Critical" threshold Astra may have hit is defined by an ability to identify and develop functional zero-day exploits of all severity levels in many hardened real-world critical systems without human intervention, or devise and execute end-to-end novel strategies for cyberattacks.
paragraph2: OpenAI says it is increasing its safeguards and security controls before deploying Astra, including limiting work on the model until new safeguards are in place. The company plans to use isolated testing environments with restricted network and tool access, along with adding sandboxed execution and more monitoring capabilities. OpenAI says it will work with relevant government agencies and AI safety organizations to test Astra. "We're committed to working alongside governments, safety institutes, and civil society to ensure that the frontier capabilities of models like Astra, and those that follow, are deployed responsibly and broadly for the benefit of all humanity," writes OpenAI. Astra wasn't formally announced, but OpenAI shared details on its next major model in a recent post outlining its mathematical advancements. Astra solved 10 open problems in math and theoretical computer science for around $2,000 (in Sol API rates). Advancements in AI are changing cybersecurity for major tech companies like Apple by unearthing an unprecedented number of bugs.

Mythos is limited to select companies because in addition to finding vulnerabilities, it has the potential to exploit them. OpenAI made headlines in July because GPT–5.6 Sol and a "more capable pre-release model" (not Astra) autonomously hacked Hugging Face during internal benchmark testing. Anthropic found Claude had done something similar. Meta this week said it too had an AI model hack another company during a cybersecurity evaluation.

title: Hero MotoCorp To Debut Maiden Electric Motorcycle Next Year
title_bn: Hero MotoCorp To Debut Maiden Electric Motorcycle Next Year
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Auto giant Hero MotoCorp is all set to unveil its first batch of electric motorcycles next year. While the company…
paragraph1: SUMMARYWhile the first product will be an electric motorcycle suited for “urban mobility”, the second one will be a high-performance e-bike catering to consumers looking for adventure This marks the first that Hero MotoCorp is foraying into the e-bike segment. This is expected to intensify competition in the space and bring more Indian two-wheeler riders into the EV fold The auto giant is timing the two launches ahead of Delhi government’s proposed ban on sale of internal combustion engine two-wheelers in the national capital from April 2028 Auto giant Hero MotoCorp is all set to unveil its first batch of electric motorcycles next year. While the company already operates in the electric vehicle (EV) segment through VIDA, this will mark the two-wheeler juggernaut’s foray into the e-bike segment. Responding to a question about the timeline of the launch of the e-bikes during Hero MotoCorp’s Q1 FY27 earnings call, the chief business officer (CBO) of the company’s emerging mobility business unit, Kausalya Nandakumar, said, “It’s not this year. We will be looking at products coming in from… next year”.
paragraph2: The legacy two-wheeler giant so far has plans to launch two electric motorcycles next year. Elaborating on this, Nandakumar said that the first product, internally code-named Project Ubex, will look to develop an electric motorcycle suited for “urban mobility”. “This will be a good performance motorcycle for consumers looking for both the thrill and acceleration of a motorcycle on an EV platform but also extremely city and road friendly”, she added. Nandakumar further added the second e-bike, code-named VXZ, will be a high-performance vehicle “catering to those consumers who are looking for adventure”. This motorcycle has been developed in collaboration with US-based Zero Motorcycles.
paragraph3: “… These are new platforms that we are developing with learnings from the scooter platform, but with technology that is suited to what a motorcycle consumer is actually looking for in terms of performance, rideability, credibility, and range,” added the CBO of Hero MotoCorp’s emerging business. The auto giant is timing the two launches ahead of Delhi government’s proposed ban on sale of internal combustion engine (ICE) two-wheelers in the national capital from April 2028. “Coming to product portfolio, way before this policy goes into effect, we will have a range of motorcycles in the market. And we are progressing well on that,” said Hero MotoCorp CEO Harshavardhan Chitale. This marks the first that the legacy giant is foraying into the e-bike segment even as it works to develop the technology.
paragraph4: The electric two-wheeler (E2W) market is currently dominated by e-scooters, with e-motorcycles accounting for a minuscule share. Within this emerging market, a wave of new-age players have spawned to cater to the growing consumer need for electric motorcycles. Ultraviolette, known for its high-performance electric bike called F77, continues to attract major institutional funding. Meanwhile, other smaller players such as Oben Electric and Matter Motor have also also rolled out e-bikes to carve a niche in the space. However, the e-bike ecosystem continues to be marred by engineering challenges, high purchase prices and lacklustre resale value.
paragraph5: Nevertheless, the entry of Hero MotoCorp and the launch of new electric bikes could intensify the competition and bring more riders from the mainstream ICE ecosystem. This comes even as E2W registrations jumped 85% to 1.91 Lakh units in July this year from 1.03 Lakh units in the same period last year. At the heart of all this is the Indian EV market, which is projected to become a $132 Bn opportunity by 2030.

title: Fenix Flexin isn’t even denying using AI to make ‘Rubberz’ anymore
title_bn: Fenix Flexin isn’t even denying using AI to make ‘Rubberz’ anymore
author: TechPulse
excerpt: It took long enough, but now LA rapper Fenix Flexin appears to have admitted using AI for the 80s synth pop-themed song "Rubberz." His comments follow the producer Medasin's videos claiming that an AI tool called Treblo (formerly Sonauto) was used to
paragraph1: Fenix now claims he’s ‘never said I didn’t use AI,‘ to make his hit song.Fenix now claims he’s ‘never said I didn’t use AI,‘ to make his hit song.by Terrence O'BrienAug 7, 2026, 8:01 PM UTCTerrence O'Brien is the Verge’s weekend editor.
paragraph2: He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.It took long enough, but now LA rapper Fenix Flexin appears to have admitted using AI for the 80s synth pop-themed song “Rubberz.” His comments follow the producer Medasin’s videos claiming that an AI tool called Treblo (formerly Sonauto) was used to make the song, and the company releasing an AI detector that identifies it as Treblo AI-created.
paragraph3: In a reply to a comment pointing out that Tyga admitted to relying on AI for his own controversial ’80s-influenced album $tarface, on one of his Instagram posts, Fenix said:never said I didn’t use AI , i said it had nun to do w recording process . I didn’t even know what da app was till we mixed it and erbody started commenting . ain’t nothing wrong w using new technology as a tool keep up w the times or get left behindThe comment insists he never denied using AI, but last month on Hot 97’s Mornings With Mero when asked directly about AI use by interviewer Kazeem Famuyide, he stated clearly that there’s “no AI on it.
paragraph4: ”He’s repeatedly gone out of his way to try and dispel the AI allegations publicly since the song was released, despite what he says now. Fenix and his team have posted what they claimed were clips of the recording session files, popped into the comments to insist the song was made by two humans recording in his living room with “pro tools auto tune and some reverb,” and said he’s actually singing in clips where it looks like he’s lip syncing.Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.

title: Check out the latest Pixel Watch apps to get a new look for their icons
title_bn: Check out the latest Pixel Watch apps to get a new look for their icons
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Google quietly rolls out new Wear OS Clock and Stopwatch icons ahead of the Pixel Watch 5.
paragraph1: Rita El Khoury / Android AuthorityTL;DR Google’s freshening up its icons for a couple Wear OS apps on Pixel Watches. Both Clock and Stopwatch are getting new colors that feel a bit more natural. These changes follow Google updating the ECG icon back in June. Google’s next smartwatch is just days away, with the Pixel Watch 5 set to go official next Wednesday alongside the new Pixel 11 series.
paragraph2: Obviously, we’re looking forward to it arriving with Wear OS 7, but it seems that Google’s also been preparing some additional tweaks to its smartwatch software portfolio, and today we’re checking out a new look for a couple of those apps.Pull up your Pixel Watch today, and chances are you’ll see an app view much like the one below:But now, ahead of the Pixel Watch 5 even getting here, Google already appears to be updating a few of these. X user Joe Lenington shares with that they’ve spotted some updated icons showing up for the Wear OS Clock and Stopwatch apps:Clock gets arguably the biggest changes here, picking up both a revised design and a tweaked color palette. The old-school alarm bells now appear a lot less prominent, and perhaps as a result, the whole thing just looks much less goofy to our eyes.
paragraph3: Google also adopts the classic 10:10 hand positioning for its new layout. Once you get used to the darker new appearance, at least, this one feels like a legit upgrade.The Stopwatch changes are a bit more subtle, and we’re really just getting some new colors for the existing design. While the old look was fine, it now almost feels like a negative version of this new icon, which we’re also fast fans of.
paragraph4: These aren’t the first Wear OS app icons that Google’s been giving some design attention to in recent months, updating its ECG app back in early June. Considering just how much work Google’s been putting into icon redesigns lately, we wouldn’t be surprised if these are far from the last Wear OS apps to try on a new look this summer.FollowThank you for being part of our community. title_bn: Apple Rumored to Launch Three New 'Ultra' Products by Early Next Year
author: TechPulse
excerpt: According to various reports from sources such as Bloomberg's Mark Gurman and Macworld's Filipe Espósito, Apple is planning to release up to three new products with "Ultra" branding between late 2026 and early 2027. The long-rumored foldable iPhone i
paragraph1: According to various reports from sources such as Bloomberg's Mark Gurman and Macworld's Filipe Espósito, Apple is planning to release up to three new products with "Ultra" branding between late 2026 and early 2027. The long-rumored foldable iPhone is expected to be called the "iPhone Ultra." Rumored features include a 7.7-inch inner display, a 5.3-inch outer display, two rear cameras, one front camera, a Touch ID power button instead of Face ID, and more. The device's large inner screen will be ideal for watching videos and multitasking. Apple is expected to release the "iPhone Ultra" this September, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.
paragraph2: In the U.S., it has been estimated that the device will have a starting price of anywhere from $1,999 to $2,499. "AirPods Ultra" are reportedly set to be released as early as this year — it would be fitting for them to be unveiled alongside the "iPhone Ultra" this September. "AirPods Ultra" are essentially rumored to be AirPods Pro with tiny infrared cameras that serve as eyes for Siri. The cameras will help to enhance the Visual Intelligence feature on the iPhone 15 Pro and newer, and a small LED light on the earbuds will indicate when the cameras are active, according to Gurman's reporting. On iOS 27, Visual Intelligence is accessible through the Camera app via a new "Siri" mode.
paragraph3: "AirPods Ultra" would provide a more hands-free experience. "The idea is to let users ask questions about an item they might be looking at," he said. If someone is looking at ingredients on their kitchen countertop, for example, they could ask Siri for dinner ideas. Last month, Apple's code for the second iOS 27 developer beta seemingly hinted at AirPods with cameras, so a launch could be fast approaching. Finally, Apple is reportedly planning a "MacBook Ultra" with an OLED display that doubles as a touch screen. Other rumored features include M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, a Dynamic Island, a thinner design compared to the latest MacBook Pro models, and potentially even an Apple-designed C2 modem for built-in 5G/LTE cellular connectivity. Apple plans to release this new MacBook by early 2027, according to Gurman.
paragraph4: All in all, Apple is expected to release an iPhone Ultra, AirPods Ultra, and a MacBook Ultra over the course of the next six to seven months or so. title: The ultimate eclipse chase: A Concorde raced against the Moon's shadow
title_bn: The ultimate eclipse chase: A Concorde raced against the Moon's shadow
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Fitted with telescopes, the plane did our longest imaging of the Sun's corona.
paragraph1: With his plan accepted, Léna began organizing experiments for the historic flight. Flying at nearly 17 km above the Earth’s surface had many benefits. “Flying very high in the stratosphere had several advantages, including no humidity, which meant an excellent infrared transmission of the solar light.
paragraph2: ” “I had planned an experiment to study the particles of dust in the corona in the infrared wavelengths. However, it would have been presumptuous to use this big aircraft only for a single experiment. So the first thing we did, after we got a feeling that the project would go ahead, was to propose to other scientific groups in France, the UK, and the United States a seat on this flight to carry their own observations,” he said.
paragraph3: Building a team While Léna was from the Paris Observatory, the other scientists came from the French National Centre for Scientific Research; Queen Mary College in London; Kitt Peak Observatory in Arizona; Los Alamos National Laboratory; and the University of Aberdeen. The main goal of this project was to use the long totality to study the solar corona at different wavelengths, as the whole corona is only visible during a total eclipse. According to Léna, the experiments included studying the dust in the corona (which was emitting infrared radiation), studying the oscillating hot gas in the corona, and studying the chromosphere.
paragraph4: To accommodate these experiments, the Concorde 001 prototype underwent significant modifications, notably the creation of four portholes in the ceiling, with one dedicated window for each experiment. Those portholes are unmissable even today. They can be seen while walking down the aisle of the aircraft.
paragraph5: With the experiments and the team of scientists chosen, two rehearsal flights were conducted before the actual flight, which took off from Las Palmas in the Canary Islands for a rendezvous with the eclipse shadow over Mauritania.

title: Watching Roku’s AI channel is like eating from a trough
title_bn: Watching Roku’s AI channel is like eating from a trough
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The appeal of free ad-supported streaming television (FAST) channels has always been the way they make it easier to (re)discover classic films and series. But Roku's latest experiment in the FAST space has less to do with traditionally produced enter
paragraph1: The appeal of free ad-supported streaming television (FAST) channels has always been the way they make it easier to (re)discover classic films and series. But Roku’s latest experiment in the FAST space has less to do with traditionally produced entertainment and is entirely focused on giving viewers access to a constant source of AI-generated content.This week, Roku added four new channels to its library of streamable programming. Along with dedicated feeds for old episodes of Mad TV, Whose Line Is It Anyway?, and a variety of Black sitcoms, the platform also debuted a 24/7 stream filled with projects from Colin Petrie-Norris’ AI startup, Fairground. Partnering with Roku is a significant step up for Fairground, which launched in 2025 and is reportedly working on its own AI-generated adaptations of Robin Hood and Dracula.
paragraph2: But watching the Fairground channel, you get the distinct sense that Roku hasn’t really gotten all that much out of the deal aside from the ability to say that it’s getting in on the gen AI craze.Like all FAST channels, Fairground AI Creator TV is filled with a curated selection of programming that you’re meant to watch somewhat passively. While you can scrub forward and backward a few seconds, there’s no way to choose exactly what kinds of videos the channel serves up. That might add a fun sense of discovery to the channel if it featured series and films that were actually riveting. But everything that I saw while watching for about an hour was more or less the same kind of short-form slop that text-to-video models have become known for.Aside from being produced with AI, there’s no consistent theme or genre to any of Fairground’s programming — all of which is made by a selection of content creators who have partnered with the company.
paragraph3: Some videos are clearly generated by models trained on footage ripped from professionally produced anime, while others just look like terrible “lifelike” CGI. Surprisingly, there were semi-cohesive narratives to some of what I watched. I could follow what was going on in a “live-action” horror about people destroying a demon by making fun of it, and I got the sense that a fantasy about Greek heroes might have been inspired by The Odyssey.Image: Roku / FairgroundYou can tell from the videos’ length and the way their audio is mixed that there was some degree of post-production editing. But the videos’ general lack of visual polish makes it obvious that they were cobbled together from machine-generated clips rather than shots crafted by a human artist. And the overall shoddiness of Fairground’s programming becomes especially apparent whenever the stream cuts to an ad — this is a FAST channel — for one of the traditionally produced movies and shows Roku offers.
paragraph4: Fairground’s website makes a point of emphasizing that it pays its content partners for their generations in addition to giving them an undisclosed share of the platform’s revenue. There’s no mention of which models are used to create Fairground’s content or whether it secured rights to use whatever training data is in the mix. But Fairground does stress that its programming is designed for “the living room, not the feed,” which says a lot about what kind of niche Petrie-Norris and his team are trying to carve out.Most AI production startups have framed themselves as being poised to revolutionize the entertainment industry with technologies that will render traditional production workflows obsolete. Generally, the “Hollywood is so cooked” set insists that AI will soon be able to churn out films and shows comparable to a major studio’s, but that doesn’t really seem like the approach Fairground is leaning into. Rather than trying to be just as good or better than regular programming, it feels like Fairground simply wants its content to exist in the same general space as stuff that people might intentionally go looking for.
paragraph5: Apparently, Roku thinks Fairground’s offerings are good enough to be platformed, which is depressing, but not altogether shocking as the company enters its Fox era.Fairgrounds’ content isn’t at all impressive, but its presence on Roku gives the startup a way to reach a massive audience of potential viewers. It’s easy to imagine an AI company seeing a business opportunity in the “looking for something mindless to play in the background” crowd, but this stuff doesn’t feel like something anyone would want to put on.Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.

title: OpenAI puts the brakes on a new model because it’s supposedly too powerful
title_bn: OpenAI puts the brakes on a new model because it’s supposedly too powerful
author: TechPulse
excerpt: OpenAI says it is pausing "internal activities" around an in-development AI model, Astra, because it doesn't yet meet new security standards the company is putting in place. The announcement follows its recent disclosure that OpenAI models accidental
paragraph1: OpenAI says its in-development Astra model may have ‘critical’ cybersecurity capabilities.OpenAI says its in-development Astra model may have ‘critical’ cybersecurity capabilities.by Jay PetersAug 7, 2026, 6:40 PM UTCImage: The VergeJay Peters is a senior reporter covering technology, gaming, and more.
paragraph2: He joined The Verge in 2019 after nearly two years at Techmeme.OpenAI says it is pausing “internal activities” around an in-development AI model, Astra, because it doesn’t yet meet new security standards the company is putting in place. The announcement follows its recent disclosure that OpenAI models accidentally hacked Hugging Face.
paragraph3: Anthropic and Meta have also since admitted that they had AI models that went rogue and breached other organizations.Recent internal evaluations of an OpenAI model called Astra indicate that it offers “significant advancements in agentic coding and cybersecurity,” according to the company. “These results, in addition to expert assessments, have led us to conclude last night that we cannot rule out critical cyber capabilities under our Preparedness Framework⁠.
paragraph4: ”Here is how OpenAI defines a “critical” cybersecurity threshold:Under our Preparedness Framework, a model reaches the Critical cybersecurity threshold if it can identify and develop functional zero-day exploits of all severity levels in many hardened real-world critical systems without human intervention, or can devise and execute end-to-end novel strategies for cyberattacks against hardened targets given only a high level desired goal.Astra was “not involved” in the Hugging Face breach, OpenAI says.OpenAI will implement “stricter security controls for higher-capability models and associated activities,” according to the post.
paragraph5: For Astra, it has also implemented “universal monitoring” for “risky actions and misalignment across all agentic applications.”Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.Jay PetersThe Verge DailyA free daily digest of the news that matters most.
